lines.text: Technician answers. T1 - Commission's Rules.
Group T1A.
Which of the following is part of the Basis and Purpose of the Amateur Radio Service? Advancing skills in the technical and communication phases of the radio art.
lines.q: Which of the following is part of the Basis and Purpose of the Amateur Radio Service?
lines.a: Advancing skills in the technical and communication phases of the radio art.

lines.text: Which agency regulates and enforces the rules for the Amateur Radio Service in the United States? The FCC.
lines.q: Which agency regulates and enforces the rules for the Amateur Radio Service in the United States?
lines.a: The FCC.

lines.text: What do the FCC rules state regarding the use of a phonetic alphabet for station identification in the Amateur Radio Service? It is encouraged when using phone emissions.
lines.q: What do the FCC rules state regarding the use of a phonetic alphabet for station identification in the Amateur Radio Service?
lines.a: It is encouraged when using phone emissions.

lines.text: How do you receive official notification of your new license and call sign after passing the exam? Email from the FCC with a link to download the license grant.
lines.q: How do you receive official notification of your new license and call sign after passing the exam?
lines.a: Email from the FCC with a link to download the license grant.

lines.text: What proves that the FCC has issued an operator/primary license grant? The license appears in the FCC ULS database.
lines.q: What proves that the FCC has issued an operator/primary license grant?
lines.a: The license appears in the FCC ULS database.

lines.text: On which of the following HF frequencies can automatically controlled amateur propagation beacons be found? On ten meters, between 28.200 MHz and 28.300 MHz.
lines.q: On which of the following HF frequencies can automatically controlled amateur propagation beacons be found?
lines.a: On ten meters, between 28.200 MHz and 28.300 MHz.

lines.text: What is the FCC Part 97 definition of a space station? An amateur station located more than 50 km above Earth's surface.
lines.q: What is the FCC Part 97 definition of a space station?
lines.a: An amateur station located more than 50 km above Earth's surface.

lines.text: Who recommends transmit/receive channels for repeater and auxiliary stations? A Volunteer Frequency Coordinator recognized by local amateurs.
lines.q: Who recommends transmit/receive channels for repeater and auxiliary stations?
lines.a: A Volunteer Frequency Coordinator recognized by local amateurs.

lines.text: Who selects a Frequency Coordinator? Amateur operators in a local or regional area whose stations are eligible to be repeater or auxiliary stations.
lines.q: Who selects a Frequency Coordinator?
lines.a: Amateur operators in a local or regional area whose stations are eligible to be repeater or auxiliary stations.

lines.text: Besides an FCC-issued amateur operator license, what is required to be the control operator of a Radio Amateur Civil Emergency Service (RACES) Station? Certification of current enrollment by a civil defense organization.
lines.q: Besides an FCC-issued amateur operator license, what is required to be the control operator of a Radio Amateur Civil Emergency Service (RACES) Station?
lines.a: Certification of current enrollment by a civil defense organization.

lines.text: Which of the following is prohibited? Willful or malicious interference.
lines.q: Which of the following is prohibited?
lines.a: Willful or malicious interference.

lines.text: Group T1B.
Which of the following frequency ranges are available for phone operation by Technician licensees? 28.300 MHz to 28.500 MHz.
lines.q: Which of the following frequency ranges are available for phone operation by Technician licensees?

lines.text: Which of the following U.S. amateur radio operators are allowed to contact the International Space Station (ISS) on VHF bands? Any amateur with a Technician class or higher license.
lines.q: Which of the following U.S. amateur radio operators are allowed to contact the International Space Station (ISS) on VHF bands?
lines.a: Any amateur with a Technician class or higher license.

lines.text: Which frequency is in the 6-meter amateur band? 52.525 MHz.
lines.q: Which frequency is in the 6-meter amateur band?

lines.text: Which amateur band includes 146.52 MHz? 2 meters.
lines.q: Which amateur band includes 146.52 MHz?
lines.a: 2 meters.

lines.text: Which of the following bands include frequencies where Technicians are authorized to use digital modes such as FT8? 10 meters; 6 meters; 2 meters; All these choices are correct.
lines.q: Which of the following bands include frequencies where Technicians are authorized to use digital modes such as FT8?
lines.a: 10 meters; 6 meters; 2 meters; All these choices are correct.

lines.text: On which HF bands does a Technician class operator have phone privileges? 10-meter band only.
lines.q: On which HF bands does a Technician class operator have phone privileges?
lines.a: 10-meter band only.

lines.text: Which of the following VHF/UHF band segments are limited to CW only? 50.0 MHz to 50.1 MHz and 144.0 MHz to 144.1 MHz.
lines.q: Which of the following VHF/UHF band segments are limited to CW only?
lines.a: 50.0 MHz to 50.1 MHz and 144.0 MHz to 144.1 MHz.

lines.text: How are US amateurs restricted in segments of bands where the Amateur Radio Service is secondary? U.S. amateurs may find non-amateur stations in those segments, and must avoid interfering with them.
lines.q: How are US amateurs restricted in segments of bands where the Amateur Radio Service is secondary?
lines.a: U.S. amateurs may find non-amateur stations in those segments, and must avoid interfering with them.

lines.text: Why should you not set your transmit frequency to be exactly at the edge of an amateur band or sub-band? To allow for calibration error in the transmitter frequency display; So that modulation sidebands do not extend beyond the band edge; To allow for transmitter frequency drift; All these choices are correct.
lines.q: Why should you not set your transmit frequency to be exactly at the edge of an amateur band or sub-band?
lines.a: To allow for calibration error in the transmitter frequency display; So that modulation sidebands do not extend beyond the band edge; To allow for transmitter frequency drift; All these choices are correct.

lines.text: Where may SSB phone be used in amateur bands above 50 MHz? In at least some segment of all these bands.
lines.q: Where may SSB phone be used in amateur bands above 50 MHz?
lines.a: In at least some segment of all these bands.

lines.text: What is the maximum peak envelope power output for Technician class operators in their HF band segments? 200 watts.
lines.q: What is the maximum peak envelope power output for Technician class operators in their HF band segments?
lines.a: 200 watts.

lines.text: Except for some specific restrictions, what is the maximum peak envelope power output for Technician class operators using frequencies above 30 MHz? 1500 watts.
lines.q: Except for some specific restrictions, what is the maximum peak envelope power output for Technician class operators using frequencies above 30 MHz?
lines.a: 1500 watts.

lines.text: Group T1C.
For which classes of amateur radio licenses does the FCC currently issue new licenses? Technician, General, Amateur Extra.
lines.q: For which classes of amateur radio licenses does the FCC currently issue new licenses?
lines.a: Technician, General, Amateur Extra.

lines.text: Who may select a desired call sign under the vanity call sign rules? Any licensed amateur.
lines.q: Who may select a desired call sign under the vanity call sign rules?
lines.a: Any licensed amateur.

lines.text: What types of international communications are FCC-licensed amateur radio stations permitted to make? Communications incidental to the purposes of the Amateur Radio Service and remarks of a personal character.
lines.q: What types of international communications are FCC-licensed amateur radio stations permitted to make?
lines.a: Communications incidental to the purposes of the Amateur Radio Service and remarks of a personal character.

lines.text: What may happen if the FCC is unable to reach you by email? Revocation of the station license or suspension of the operator license.
lines.q: What may happen if the FCC is unable to reach you by email?
lines.a: Revocation of the station license or suspension of the operator license.

lines.text: Which of the following is a valid Group D call sign format for Technician class? KF1XXX.
lines.q: Which of the following is a valid Group D call sign format for Technician class?
lines.a: KF1XXX.

lines.text: Which of the following statements is true about using your amateur radio license when operating aboard a vessel or craft in international waters? You may operate from a US-documented vessel with the master's permission.
lines.q: Which of the following statements is true about using your amateur radio license when operating aboard a vessel or craft in international waters?
lines.a: You may operate from a US-documented vessel with the master's permission.

lines.text: How long before the expiration date may an amateur radio license renewal be requested? 90 days.
lines.q: How long before the expiration date may an amateur radio license renewal be requested?
lines.a: 90 days.

lines.text: What is the normal term for an FCC-issued amateur radio license? Ten years.
lines.q: What is the normal term for an FCC-issued amateur radio license?
lines.a: Ten years.

lines.text: What is the grace period for renewal if an amateur license expires? Two years.
lines.q: What is the grace period for renewal if an amateur license expires?
lines.a: Two years.

lines.text: How soon after passing the examination for your first amateur radio license may you transmit on the amateur radio bands? As soon as your operator/station license grant appears in the FCC’s license database.
lines.q: How soon after passing the examination for your first amateur radio license may you transmit on the amateur radio bands?
lines.a: As soon as your operator/station license grant appears in the FCC’s license database.

lines.text: If your license has expired and is still within the allowable grace period, may you continue to transmit on the amateur radio bands? No, you must wait until the license has been renewed.
lines.q: If your license has expired and is still within the allowable grace period, may you continue to transmit on the amateur radio bands?
lines.a: No, you must wait until the license has been renewed.

lines.text: Group T1D.

With which countries are FCC-licensed amateur radio stations prohibited from exchanging communications? Any country whose administration has notified the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) that it objects to such communications.
lines.q: With which countries are FCC-licensed amateur radio stations prohibited from exchanging communications?
lines.a: Any country whose administration has notified the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) that it objects to such communications.

lines.text: Under which of the following circumstances are one-way transmissions by an amateur station prohibited? Broadcasting.
lines.q: Under which of the following circumstances are one-way transmissions by an amateur station prohibited?
lines.a: Broadcasting.

lines.text: When is it permissible to transmit messages encoded to obscure their meaning? Only when transmitting control commands to space stations or model craft.
lines.q: When is it permissible to transmit messages encoded to obscure their meaning?
lines.a: Only when transmitting control commands to space stations or model craft.

lines.text: Under what conditions is an amateur station authorized to transmit music using a phone emission? When incidental to an authorized retransmission of manned spacecraft communications.
lines.q: Under what conditions is an amateur station authorized to transmit music using a phone emission?
lines.a: When incidental to an authorized retransmission of manned spacecraft communications.

lines.text: When may amateur radio operators use their stations to notify other amateurs of the availability of equipment for sale or trade? When selling amateur radio equipment and not on a regular basis.
lines.q: When may amateur radio operators use their stations to notify other amateurs of the availability of equipment for sale or trade?
lines.a: When selling amateur radio equipment and not on a regular basis.

lines.text: What, if any, are the restrictions concerning transmission of language that may be considered indecent or obscene? Any such language is prohibited.
lines.q: What, if any, are the restrictions concerning transmission of language that may be considered indecent or obscene?
lines.a: Any such language is prohibited.

lines.text: Which of the following is an example of an auxiliary station? A station sending one-way transmissions between a remote repeater receiver and the main repeater transmitter.
lines.q: Which of the following is an example of an auxiliary station?
lines.a: A station sending one-way transmissions between a remote repeater receiver and the main repeater transmitter.

lines.text: In which of the following circumstances may the control operator of an amateur station receive compensation for operating that station? When the communication is a part of classroom instruction at an educational institution.
lines.q: In which of the following circumstances may the control operator of an amateur station receive compensation for operating that station?
lines.a: When the communication is a part of classroom instruction at an educational institution.

lines.text: When may amateur stations transmit information in support of broadcasting, program production, or news gathering, assuming no other means is available? When such communications are directly related to the immediate safety of human life or protection of property.
lines.q: When may amateur stations transmit information in support of broadcasting, program production, or news gathering, assuming no other means is available?
lines.a: When such communications are directly related to the immediate safety of human life or protection of property.

lines.text: How does the FCC define broadcasting for the Amateur Radio Service? Transmissions intended for reception by the general public.
lines.q: How does the FCC define broadcasting for the Amateur Radio Service?
lines.a: Transmissions intended for reception by the general public.

lines.text: When may an amateur station transmit without identifying on the air? When transmitting signals to control model craft.
lines.q: When may an amateur station transmit without identifying on the air?
lines.a: When transmitting signals to control model craft.

lines.text: Which of the following is required when making on-the-air test transmissions? Identify the transmitting station.
lines.q: Which of the following is required when making on-the-air test transmissions?
lines.a: Identify the transmitting station.

lines.text: Group T1E.
When may an amateur station transmit without a control operator? Never.
lines.q: When may an amateur station transmit without a control operator?
lines.a: Never.

lines.text: Who may be the control operator of a station communicating through an amateur satellite or space station? Any amateur allowed to transmit on the satellite uplink frequency.
lines.q: Who may be the control operator of a station communicating through an amateur satellite or space station?
lines.a: Any amateur allowed to transmit on the satellite uplink frequency.

lines.text: Who must designate the station control operator? The station licensee.
lines.q: Who must designate the station control operator?
lines.a: The station licensee.

lines.text: What determines the transmitting frequency privileges of an amateur station? The class of operator license held by the control operator.
lines.q: What determines the transmitting frequency privileges of an amateur station?
lines.a: The class of operator license held by the control operator.

lines.text: What is an amateur station’s control point? The location at which the control operator function is performed.
lines.q: What is an amateur station’s control point?
lines.a: The location at which the control operator function is performed.

lines.text: When, other than during an emergency, may a Technician class licensee be the control operator of a station operating in an Amateur Extra Class band segment? At no time.
lines.q: When, other than during an emergency, may a Technician class licensee be the control operator of a station operating in an Amateur Extra Class band segment?
lines.a: At no time.

lines.text: When the control operator is not the station licensee, who is responsible for the proper operation of the station? The control operator and the station licensee.
lines.q: When the control operator is not the station licensee, who is responsible for the proper operation of the station?
lines.a: The control operator and the station licensee.

lines.text: Which of the following is an example of automatic control? Repeater operation.
lines.q: Which of the following is an example of automatic control?
lines.a: Repeater operation.

lines.text: Which amateur stations may be remotely controlled? Any station.
lines.q: Which amateur stations may be remotely controlled?
lines.a: Any station.

lines.text: Which of the following is an example of remote control as defined in Part 97? Operating the station over the internet.
lines.q: Which of the following is an example of remote control as defined in Part 97?
lines.a: Operating the station over the internet.

lines.text: What is a control operator as defined in Part 97? An amateur operator designated by the licensee of a station to be responsible for transmissions and FCC rules compliance at that station.
lines.q: What is a control operator as defined in Part 97?
lines.a: An amateur operator designated by the licensee of a station to be responsible for transmissions and FCC rules compliance at that station.

lines.text: Group T1F.
When must the station licensee make the station and the station records available for inspection? At any time upon request by an FCC representative.
lines.q: When must the station licensee make the station and the station records available for inspection?
lines.a: At any time upon request by an FCC representative.

lines.text: How often must you identify with your FCC-assigned call sign when using tactical call signs such as “Race Headquarters”? At least every 10 minutes during and at the end of a communication.
lines.q: How often must you identify with your FCC-assigned call sign when using tactical call signs such as “Race Headquarters”?
lines.a: At least every 10 minutes during and at the end of a communication.

lines.text: When are you required to transmit your assigned call sign? At least every 10 minutes during and at the end of a communication.
lines.q: When are you required to transmit your assigned call sign?
lines.a: At least every 10 minutes during and at the end of a communication.

lines.text: What language must you use for identification when using a phone emission? English.
lines.q: What language must you use for identification when using a phone emission?
lines.a: English.

lines.text: What method of call sign identification is required for a station transmitting phone signals? Send the call sign using a CW or phone emission.
lines.q: What method of call sign identification is required for a station transmitting phone signals?
lines.a: Send the call sign using a CW or phone emission.

lines.text: Which of the following self-assigned indicators are acceptable when using a phone transmission? KL7CC stroke W3; KL7CC slant W3; KL7CC slash W3; All these choices are correct.
lines.q: Which of the following self-assigned indicators are acceptable when using a phone transmission?
lines.a: KL7CC stroke W3; KL7CC slant W3; KL7CC slash W3; All these choices are correct.

lines.text: Which of the following restrictions apply when a non-licensed person speaks to a foreign amateur radio station via a station under the control of an FCC-licensed amateur radio operator? The foreign station must be in a country with which the U.S. has a third-party agreement.
lines.q: Which of the following restrictions apply when a non-licensed person speaks to a foreign amateur radio station via a station under the control of an FCC-licensed amateur radio operator?
lines.a: The foreign station must be in a country with which the U.S. has a third-party agreement.

lines.text: What is the definition of third-party communications? A message from a control operator to another amateur station control operator on behalf of another person.
lines.q: What is the definition of third-party communications?
lines.a: A message from a control operator to another amateur station control operator on behalf of another person.

lines.text: What type of amateur station simultaneously retransmits the signal of another amateur station on a different channel or channels? Repeater station.
lines.q: What type of amateur station simultaneously retransmits the signal of another amateur station on a different channel or channels?
lines.a: Repeater station.

lines.text: Who is accountable if a repeater inadvertently retransmits communications that violate the FCC rules? The control operator of the originating station.
lines.q: Who is accountable if a repeater inadvertently retransmits communications that violate the FCC rules?
lines.a: The control operator of the originating station.

lines.text: Which of the following is a requirement for the issuance of a club station license grant? The club must have at least four members.
lines.q: Which of the following is a requirement for the issuance of a club station license grant?
lines.a: The club must have at least four members.

lines.text: Technician answers. T2 - Operating Procedures.
Group T2A.
What is a common repeater frequency offset in the 2-meter band? Plus or minus 600 kHz.
lines.q: What is a common repeater frequency offset in the 2-meter band?
lines.a: Plus or minus 600 kHz.

lines.text: What is the national calling frequency for FM simplex operations in the 2-meter band? 146.520 MHz.
lines.q: What is the national calling frequency for FM simplex operations in the 2-meter band?

lines.text: What is a common repeater frequency offset in the 70-centimeter band? Plus or minus 5 MHz.
lines.q: What is a common repeater frequency offset in the 70-centimeter band?
lines.a: Plus or minus 5 MHz.

lines.text: What is an appropriate way to call another station on a repeater if you know the other station's call sign? Say the station's call sign, then identify with your call sign.
lines.q: What is an appropriate way to call another station on a repeater if you know the other station's call sign?
lines.a: Say the station's call sign, then identify with your call sign.

lines.text: How should you respond to a station calling CQ? Transmit the other station’s call sign followed by your call sign.
lines.q: How should you respond to a station calling CQ?
lines.a: Transmit the other station’s call sign followed by your call sign.

lines.text: What is an effective way to seek a call from any phone station when not using a repeater? Repeat “CQ” a few times, followed by “this is,” and your call sign, then pause to listen; repeat as necessary.
lines.q: What is an effective way to seek a call from any phone station when not using a repeater?
lines.a: Repeat “CQ” a few times, followed by “this is,” and your call sign, then pause to listen; repeat as necessary.

lines.text: What does the term "repeater offset" mean? The difference between a repeater’s transmit and receive frequencies.
lines.q: What does the term "repeater offset" mean?
lines.a: The difference between a repeater’s transmit and receive frequencies.

lines.text: What is the meaning of the procedural signal “CQ”? Calling any station.
lines.q: What is the meaning of the procedural signal “CQ”?
lines.a: Calling any station.

lines.text: Which of the following is a customary way to indicate a station is listening on a repeater and looking for a contact? The station’s call sign followed by the word “listening”.
lines.q: Which of the following is a customary way to indicate a station is listening on a repeater and looking for a contact?
lines.a: The station’s call sign followed by the word “listening”.

lines.text: What is a band plan, beyond the privileges established by the FCC? A voluntary guideline for using different modes or activities within an amateur band.
lines.q: What is a band plan, beyond the privileges established by the FCC?
lines.a: A voluntary guideline for using different modes or activities within an amateur band.

lines.text: What term describes an amateur station that is transmitting and receiving on the same frequency? Simplex.
lines.q: What term describes an amateur station that is transmitting and receiving on the same frequency?
lines.a: Simplex.

lines.text: Group T2B.
What is the purpose of the reverse function on a VHF/UHF transceiver? To listen on a repeater’s input frequency.
lines.q: What is the purpose of the reverse function on a VHF/UHF transceiver?
lines.a: To listen on a repeater’s input frequency.

lines.text: What term describes the use of a sub-audible tone transmitted along with normal voice audio to open the squelch of a receiver? CTCSS.
lines.q: What term describes the use of a sub-audible tone transmitted along with normal voice audio to open the squelch of a receiver?
lines.a: CTCSS.

lines.text: Which of the following describes a linked repeater network? A network of repeaters in which signals received by one repeater are transmitted by all the repeaters in the network.
lines.q: Which of the following describes a linked repeater network?
lines.a: A network of repeaters in which signals received by one repeater are transmitted by all the repeaters in the network.

lines.text: Which of the following could be the reason you are unable to access a repeater whose output you can hear? Improper transceiver offset; You are using the wrong CTCSS tone; You are using the wrong DCS code; All these choices are correct.
lines.q: Which of the following could be the reason you are unable to access a repeater whose output you can hear?
lines.a: Improper transceiver offset; You are using the wrong CTCSS tone; You are using the wrong DCS code; All these choices are correct.

lines.text: Which of the following would cause your FM transmission audio to drop out on voice peaks? You are talking too loudly.
lines.q: Which of the following would cause your FM transmission audio to drop out on voice peaks?
lines.a: You are talking too loudly.

lines.text: What type of signaling to a repeater uses two simultaneous audio tones? DTMF.
lines.q: What type of signaling to a repeater uses two simultaneous audio tones?
lines.a: DTMF.

lines.text: How can you join a digital repeater’s “talkgroup”? Program your radio with the group’s ID or code.
lines.q: How can you join a digital repeater’s “talkgroup”?
lines.a: Program your radio with the group’s ID or code.

lines.text: Which of the following applies when two stations transmitting on the same frequency interfere with each other? The stations should negotiate continued use of the frequency.
lines.q: Which of the following applies when two stations transmitting on the same frequency interfere with each other?
lines.a: The stations should negotiate continued use of the frequency.

lines.text: Why are simplex channels designated in the VHF/UHF band plans? So stations within range of each other can communicate without tying up a repeater.
lines.q: Why are simplex channels designated in the VHF/UHF band plans?
lines.a: So stations within range of each other can communicate without tying up a repeater.

lines.text: Which Q signal indicates that you are receiving interference from other stations? QRM.
lines.q: Which Q signal indicates that you are receiving interference from other stations?
lines.a: QRM.

lines.text: Which Q signal indicates that you are changing frequency? QSY.
lines.q: Which Q signal indicates that you are changing frequency?
lines.a: QSY.

lines.text: What is the digital color code used on DMR repeater systems? An access code which must be programmed into a DMR transmitter to access a specific repeater.
lines.q: What is the digital color code used on DMR repeater systems?
lines.a: An access code which must be programmed into a DMR transmitter to access a specific repeater.

lines.text: What is the purpose of a squelch function? Mute the receiver audio when a signal is not present.
lines.q: What is the purpose of a squelch function?
lines.a: Mute the receiver audio when a signal is not present.

lines.text: Which of the following is a “talkgroup”? An identifier used by DMR to organize radio traffic so that those who want to hear the group aren’t bothered by other radio traffic.
lines.q: Which of the following is a “talkgroup”?
lines.a: An identifier used by DMR to organize radio traffic so that those who want to hear the group aren’t bothered by other radio traffic.

lines.text: Group T2C.
When do the FCC Part 97 Amateur Radio Service rules NOT apply to the operation of an amateur station? FCC rules always apply.
lines.q: When do the FCC Part 97 Amateur Radio Service rules NOT apply to the operation of an amateur station?
lines.a: FCC rules always apply.

lines.text: Which of the following are typical duties of a Net Control Station? Call the net to order and direct communications between stations checking in.
lines.q: Which of the following are typical duties of a Net Control Station?
lines.a: Call the net to order and direct communications between stations checking in.

lines.text: What technique is used to ensure that voice messages containing unusual words are received correctly? Spell the words using a standard phonetic alphabet.
lines.q: What technique is used to ensure that voice messages containing unusual words are received correctly?
lines.a: Spell the words using a standard phonetic alphabet.

lines.text: What is RACES? An FCC Part 97 amateur radio service for civil defense communications during national emergencies.
lines.q: What is RACES?
lines.a: An FCC Part 97 amateur radio service for civil defense communications during national emergencies.

lines.text: What does the term “traffic” refer to in net operation? Formal messages exchanged by net stations.
lines.q: What does the term “traffic” refer to in net operation?
lines.a: Formal messages exchanged by net stations.

lines.text: What is the Amateur Radio Emergency Service (ARES)? A group of licensed amateurs who have voluntarily registered their qualifications and equipment for communications duty in the public service.
lines.q: What is the Amateur Radio Emergency Service (ARES)?
lines.a: A group of licensed amateurs who have voluntarily registered their qualifications and equipment for communications duty in the public service.

lines.text: Which of the following is standard practice when you participate in a net? Unless you are reporting an emergency, transmit only when directed by the net control station.
lines.q: Which of the following is standard practice when you participate in a net?
lines.a: Unless you are reporting an emergency, transmit only when directed by the net control station.

lines.text: Which of the following relays messages using email addresses based on amateur callsigns? Winlink.
lines.q: Which of the following relays messages using email addresses based on amateur callsigns?
lines.a: Winlink.

lines.text: Are amateur station control operators ever permitted to operate outside the frequency privileges of their license class? Yes, but only in situations involving the immediate safety of human life or protection of property.
lines.q: Are amateur station control operators ever permitted to operate outside the frequency privileges of their license class?
lines.a: Yes, but only in situations involving the immediate safety of human life or protection of property.

lines.text: What information is contained in the preamble of a formal traffic message? Information needed to track the message.
lines.q: What information is contained in the preamble of a formal traffic message?
lines.a: Information needed to track the message.

lines.text: What is meant by “check” in a radiogram header? The number of words or word equivalents in the text portion of the message.
lines.q: What is meant by “check” in a radiogram header?
lines.a: The number of words or word equivalents in the text portion of the message.

lines.text: Which of the following requires certification by a civil defense agency? RACES.
lines.q: Which of the following requires certification by a civil defense agency?
lines.a: RACES.

lines.text: Technician answers. T3 - Radio Wave Propagation.
Group T3A.
Why do VHF signal strengths sometimes vary greatly when the antenna is moved only a few feet? Multipath propagation cancels or reinforces signals.
lines.q: Why do VHF signal strengths sometimes vary greatly when the antenna is moved only a few feet?
lines.a: Multipath propagation cancels or reinforces signals.

lines.text: How does vegetation affect UHF and microwave signals? Absorbs signals, leading to poor reception of weak signals.
lines.q: How does vegetation affect UHF and microwave signals?
lines.a: Absorbs signals, leading to poor reception of weak signals.

lines.text: What antenna polarization is normally used for long-distance CW and SSB contacts on the VHF and UHF bands? Horizontal.
lines.q: What antenna polarization is normally used for long-distance CW and SSB contacts on the VHF and UHF bands?
lines.a: Horizontal.

lines.text: What is the effect of antenna cross-polarization over a line-of-sight VHF or UHF path? Received signal strength is reduced.
lines.q: What is the effect of antenna cross-polarization over a line-of-sight VHF or UHF path?
