Which of the following is a safety hazard of a 12-volt storage battery that lacks internal protection circuitry? Shorting the terminals can cause burns, fire, or an explosion.
lines.q: Which of the following is a safety hazard of a 12-volt storage battery that lacks internal protection circuitry?
lines.a: Shorting the terminals can cause burns, fire, or an explosion.

lines.text: What health hazard is posed by electrical current flowing through the body? It may cause injury by heating body tissue; It may disrupt the electrical functions of cells; It may cause involuntary muscle contractions; All these choices are correct.
lines.q: What health hazard is posed by electrical current flowing through the body?
lines.a: It may cause injury by heating body tissue; It may disrupt the electrical functions of cells; It may cause involuntary muscle contractions; All these choices are correct.

lines.text: In the United States, what circuit does black wire insulation indicate in a three-wire 120 V AC cable? Hot.
lines.q: In the United States, what circuit does black wire insulation indicate in a three-wire 120 V AC cable?
lines.a: Hot.

lines.text: What is the purpose of a fuse in an electrical circuit? To remove power in case of an overload.
lines.q: What is the purpose of a fuse in an electrical circuit?
lines.a: To remove power in case of an overload.

lines.text: Why should a 5-ampere fuse never be replaced with a 20-ampere fuse? Excessive current could cause a fire.
lines.q: Why should a 5-ampere fuse never be replaced with a 20-ampere fuse?
lines.a: Excessive current could cause a fire.

lines.text: What is a good way to guard against electrical shock at your station? Use three-wire cords and plugs for all AC powered equipment; Connect all AC powered station equipment to a common safety ground; Ensure all capacitors used for high-voltage DC are fully discharged before working inside equipment; All these choices are correct.
lines.q: What is a good way to guard against electrical shock at your station?
lines.a: Use three-wire cords and plugs for all AC powered equipment; Connect all AC powered station equipment to a common safety ground; Ensure all capacitors used for high-voltage DC are fully discharged before working inside equipment; All these choices are correct.

lines.text: Where should a lightning arrester be installed in a coaxial feed line? On a grounded panel near where feed lines enter the building.
lines.q: Where should a lightning arrester be installed in a coaxial feed line?
lines.a: On a grounded panel near where feed lines enter the building.

lines.text: Where should a fuse or circuit breaker be installed in a 120V AC power circuit? In series with the hot conductor only.
lines.q: Where should a fuse or circuit breaker be installed in a 120V AC power circuit?
lines.a: In series with the hot conductor only.

lines.text: What should be done to all external ground rods or earth connections? Bond them together with heavy wire or conductive strap.
lines.q: What should be done to all external ground rods or earth connections?
lines.a: Bond them together with heavy wire or conductive strap.

lines.text: What hazard exists when rapidly charging or discharging an unprotected battery? Overheating or out-gassing.
lines.q: What hazard exists when rapidly charging or discharging an unprotected battery?
lines.a: Overheating or out-gassing.

lines.text: What hazard exists in a power supply immediately after turning it off? Charge stored in filter capacitors.
lines.q: What hazard exists in a power supply immediately after turning it off?
lines.a: Charge stored in filter capacitors.

lines.text: Which of the following precautions should be taken when measuring high voltages with a voltmeter? Ensure that the voltmeter and its leads are rated for use at the voltages being measured.
lines.q: Which of the following precautions should be taken when measuring high voltages with a voltmeter?
lines.a: Ensure that the voltmeter and its leads are rated for use at the voltages being measured.

lines.text: Group T0B.
Which of the following is good practice when installing ground wires on a tower for lightning protection? Ensure that connections are short and direct.
lines.q: Which of the following is good practice when installing ground wires on a tower for lightning protection?
lines.a: Ensure that connections are short and direct.

lines.text: What is required when climbing an antenna tower? Have sufficient training on safe tower climbing techniques; Use appropriate tie-off to the tower at all times; Always wear an approved climbing harness; All these choices are correct.
lines.q: What is required when climbing an antenna tower?
lines.a: Have sufficient training on safe tower climbing techniques; Use appropriate tie-off to the tower at all times; Always wear an approved climbing harness; All these choices are correct.

lines.text: Under what circumstances is it safe to climb a tower without a helper or observer? Never.
lines.q: Under what circumstances is it safe to climb a tower without a helper or observer?
lines.a: Never.

lines.text: Which of the following is an important safety precaution to observe when putting up an antenna tower? Look for and stay clear of any overhead electrical wires.
lines.q: Which of the following is an important safety precaution to observe when putting up an antenna tower?
lines.a: Look for and stay clear of any overhead electrical wires.

lines.text: What is the purpose of a safety wire through a turnbuckle used to tension guy lines? Prevent loosening of the turnbuckle from vibration.
lines.q: What is the purpose of a safety wire through a turnbuckle used to tension guy lines?
lines.a: Prevent loosening of the turnbuckle from vibration.

lines.text: What is the minimum safe distance from a power line to allow when installing an antenna? Enough so that if the antenna falls, no part of it can come within 10 feet of the power wires.
lines.q: What is the minimum safe distance from a power line to allow when installing an antenna?
lines.a: Enough so that if the antenna falls, no part of it can come within 10 feet of the power wires.

lines.text: Which of the following is an important safety rule to remember when using a crank-up tower? This type of tower must not be climbed unless it is retracted, or mechanical safety locking devices have been installed.
lines.q: Which of the following is an important safety rule to remember when using a crank-up tower?
lines.a: This type of tower must not be climbed unless it is retracted, or mechanical safety locking devices have been installed.

lines.text: Which is a proper grounding method for a tower? Separate eight-foot ground rods for each tower leg, bonded to the tower and each other.
lines.q: Which is a proper grounding method for a tower?
lines.a: Separate eight-foot ground rods for each tower leg, bonded to the tower and each other.

lines.text: Why should you avoid attaching an antenna to a utility pole? The antenna could contact high-voltage power lines.
lines.q: Why should you avoid attaching an antenna to a utility pole?
lines.a: The antenna could contact high-voltage power lines.

lines.text: Which of the following is true when installing grounding conductors used for lightning protection? Sharp bends must be avoided.
lines.q: Which of the following is true when installing grounding conductors used for lightning protection?
lines.a: Sharp bends must be avoided.

lines.text: Which of the following establishes grounding requirements for an amateur radio tower or antenna? Local electrical codes.
lines.q: Which of the following establishes grounding requirements for an amateur radio tower or antenna?
lines.a: Local electrical codes.

lines.text: Group T0C.
What type of radiation are radio signals? Non-ionizing radiation.
lines.q: What type of radiation are radio signals?
lines.a: Non-ionizing radiation.

lines.text: Which of the following bands has the lowest maximum permissible exposure for RF safety? 50 MHz.
lines.q: Which of the following bands has the lowest maximum permissible exposure for RF safety?
lines.a: 50 MHz.

lines.text: How does the allowable power density for RF safety change if duty cycle changes from 100 percent to 50 percent? It increases by a factor of 2.
lines.q: How does the allowable power density for RF safety change if duty cycle changes from 100 percent to 50 percent?
lines.a: It increases by a factor of 2.

lines.text: What factors affect the RF exposure of people near an amateur station antenna? Frequency and power level of the RF field; Distance from the antenna to a person; Radiation pattern of the antenna; All these choices are correct.
lines.q: What factors affect the RF exposure of people near an amateur station antenna?
lines.a: Frequency and power level of the RF field; Distance from the antenna to a person; Radiation pattern of the antenna; All these choices are correct.

lines.text: Why do exposure limits vary with frequency? The human body absorbs more RF energy at some frequencies than at others.
lines.q: Why do exposure limits vary with frequency?
lines.a: The human body absorbs more RF energy at some frequencies than at others.

lines.text: Which of the following is an acceptable method to determine whether your station complies with FCC RF exposure regulations? By calculation based on FCC OET Bulletin 65; By calculation based on computer modeling; By measurement of field strength using calibrated equipment; All these choices are correct.
lines.q: Which of the following is an acceptable method to determine whether your station complies with FCC RF exposure regulations?
lines.a: By calculation based on FCC OET Bulletin 65; By calculation based on computer modeling; By measurement of field strength using calibrated equipment; All these choices are correct.

lines.text: What hazard is created by touching an antenna during a transmission? RF burn to skin.
lines.q: What hazard is created by touching an antenna during a transmission?
lines.a: RF burn to skin.

lines.text: Which of the following actions can reduce exposure to RF radiation? Relocate antennas.
lines.q: Which of the following actions can reduce exposure to RF radiation?
lines.a: Relocate antennas.

lines.text: How can you make sure your station stays in compliance with RF safety regulations? By re-evaluating the station whenever an item in the transmitter or antenna system is changed.
lines.q: How can you make sure your station stays in compliance with RF safety regulations?
lines.a: By re-evaluating the station whenever an item in the transmitter or antenna system is changed.

lines.text: Why is duty cycle one of the factors used to determine safe RF radiation exposure levels? It affects the average exposure to radiation.
lines.q: Why is duty cycle one of the factors used to determine safe RF radiation exposure levels?
lines.a: It affects the average exposure to radiation.

lines.text: What is the definition of duty cycle during the averaging time for RF exposure? The percentage of time that a transmitter is transmitting.
lines.q: What is the definition of duty cycle during the averaging time for RF exposure?
lines.a: The percentage of time that a transmitter is transmitting.

lines.text: How does RF radiation differ from ionizing radiation (radioactivity)? RF radiation does not have sufficient energy to cause chemical changes in cells and damage DNA.
lines.q: How does RF radiation differ from ionizing radiation (radioactivity)?
lines.a: RF radiation does not have sufficient energy to cause chemical changes in cells and damage DNA.

lines.text: Who is responsible for ensuring that no person is exposed to RF energy above the FCC exposure limits? The station licensee.
lines.q: Who is responsible for ensuring that no person is exposed to RF energy above the FCC exposure limits?
lines.a: The station licensee.

lines.text: General answers. G1 - Commission's Rules.
Group G1A.
On which HF and/or MF amateur bands are there portions where General class licensees cannot transmit? 80 meters, 40 meters, 20 meters, and 15 meters.
lines.q: On which HF and/or MF amateur bands are there portions where General class licensees cannot transmit?
lines.a: 80 meters, 40 meters, 20 meters, and 15 meters.

lines.text: On which of the following bands is phone operation prohibited? 30 meters.
lines.q: On which of the following bands is phone operation prohibited?
lines.a: 30 meters.

lines.text: On which of the following bands is image transmission prohibited? 30 meters.
lines.q: On which of the following bands is image transmission prohibited?
lines.a: 30 meters.

lines.text: On which of the following frequencies are General class licensees prohibited from operating as control operator? 7.125 MHz to 7.175 MHz.
lines.q: On which of the following frequencies are General class licensees prohibited from operating as control operator?
lines.a: 7.125 MHz to 7.175 MHz.

lines.text: Which of the following applies when the FCC rules designate the amateur service as a secondary user on a band? Amateur stations must not cause harmful interference to primary users and must accept interference from primary users.
lines.q: Which of the following applies when the FCC rules designate the amateur service as a secondary user on a band?
lines.a: Amateur stations must not cause harmful interference to primary users and must accept interference from primary users.

lines.text: On which amateur frequencies in the 10-meter band may stations with a General class control operator transmit CW emissions? The entire band.
lines.q: On which amateur frequencies in the 10-meter band may stations with a General class control operator transmit CW emissions?
lines.a: The entire band.

lines.text: Which HF bands have segments exclusively allocated to Amateur Extra licensees? 80 meters, 40 meters, 20 meters, and 15 meters.
lines.q: Which HF bands have segments exclusively allocated to Amateur Extra licensees?
lines.a: 80 meters, 40 meters, 20 meters, and 15 meters.

lines.text: Which of the following frequencies is within the General class portion of the 15-meter band? 21300 kHz.
lines.q: Which of the following frequencies is within the General class portion of the 15-meter band?

lines.text: What portion of the 10-meter band is available for repeater use? The portion above 29.5 MHz.
lines.q: What portion of the 10-meter band is available for repeater use?
lines.a: The portion above 29.5 MHz.

lines.text: When General class licensees are not permitted to use the entire voice portion of a band, which portion of the voice segment is available to them? The upper frequency portion.
lines.q: When General class licensees are not permitted to use the entire voice portion of a band, which portion of the voice segment is available to them?
lines.a: The upper frequency portion.

lines.text: Group G1B.
What is the maximum height above ground for an antenna structure not near a public use airport without requiring notification to the FAA and registration with the FCC? 200 feet.
lines.q: What is the maximum height above ground for an antenna structure not near a public use airport without requiring notification to the FAA and registration with the FCC?
lines.a: 200 feet.

lines.text: With which of the following conditions must beacon stations comply? No more than one beacon station may transmit in the same band from the same station location.
lines.q: With which of the following conditions must beacon stations comply?
lines.a: No more than one beacon station may transmit in the same band from the same station location.

lines.text: Which of the following is a purpose of a beacon station as identified in the FCC rules? Observation of propagation and reception.
lines.q: Which of the following is a purpose of a beacon station as identified in the FCC rules?
lines.a: Observation of propagation and reception.

lines.text: Which of the following transmissions is permitted for all amateur stations? Occasional retransmission of weather and propagation forecast information from US government stations.
lines.q: Which of the following transmissions is permitted for all amateur stations?
lines.a: Occasional retransmission of weather and propagation forecast information from US government stations.

lines.text: Which of the following one-way transmissions are permitted? Transmissions to assist with learning the International Morse code.
lines.q: Which of the following one-way transmissions are permitted?
lines.a: Transmissions to assist with learning the International Morse code.

lines.text: Under what conditions are state and local governments permitted to regulate amateur radio antenna structures? Amateur Service communications must be reasonably accommodated, and regulations must constitute the minimum practical to accommodate a legitimate purpose of the state or local entity.
lines.q: Under what conditions are state and local governments permitted to regulate amateur radio antenna structures?
lines.a: Amateur Service communications must be reasonably accommodated, and regulations must constitute the minimum practical to accommodate a legitimate purpose of the state or local entity.

lines.text: What are the restrictions on the use of abbreviations or procedural signals in the amateur service? They may be used if they do not obscure the meaning of a message.
lines.q: What are the restrictions on the use of abbreviations or procedural signals in the amateur service?
lines.a: They may be used if they do not obscure the meaning of a message.

lines.text: When is it permissible to communicate with amateur stations in countries outside the areas administered by the Federal Communications Commission? When the contact is with amateurs in any country except those whose administrations have notified the ITU that they object to such communications.
lines.q: When is it permissible to communicate with amateur stations in countries outside the areas administered by the Federal Communications Commission?
lines.a: When the contact is with amateurs in any country except those whose administrations have notified the ITU that they object to such communications.

lines.text: On what HF frequencies are automatically controlled beacons permitted? 28.20 MHz to 28.30 MHz.
lines.q: On what HF frequencies are automatically controlled beacons permitted?
lines.a: 28.20 MHz to 28.30 MHz.

lines.text: What is the power limit for beacon stations? 100 watts PEP output.
lines.q: What is the power limit for beacon stations?
lines.a: 100 watts PEP output.

lines.text: Who or what determines “good engineering and good amateur practice,” as applied to the operation of an amateur station in all respects not covered by the Part 97 rules? The FCC.
lines.q: Who or what determines “good engineering and good amateur practice,” as applied to the operation of an amateur station in all respects not covered by the Part 97 rules?
lines.a: The FCC.

lines.text: Group G1C.
What is the maximum transmitter power an amateur station may use on 10.140 MHz? 200 watts PEP output.
lines.q: What is the maximum transmitter power an amateur station may use on 10.140 MHz?
lines.a: 200 watts PEP output.

lines.text: What is the maximum transmitter power an amateur station may use on the 12-meter band? 1500 watts PEP output.
lines.q: What is the maximum transmitter power an amateur station may use on the 12-meter band?
lines.a: 1500 watts PEP output.

lines.text: What is the maximum bandwidth permitted by FCC rules for amateur radio stations transmitting on USB frequencies in the 60-meter band? 2.8 kHz.
lines.q: What is the maximum bandwidth permitted by FCC rules for amateur radio stations transmitting on USB frequencies in the 60-meter band?
lines.a: 2.8 kHz.

lines.text: Which of the following is required by the FCC rules when operating in the 60-meter band? If you are using an antenna other than a dipole, you must keep a record of the gain of your antenna.
lines.q: Which of the following is required by the FCC rules when operating in the 60-meter band?
lines.a: If you are using an antenna other than a dipole, you must keep a record of the gain of your antenna.

lines.text: What is the limit for transmitter power on the 28 MHz band for a General Class control operator? 1500 watts PEP output.
lines.q: What is the limit for transmitter power on the 28 MHz band for a General Class control operator?
lines.a: 1500 watts PEP output.

lines.text: What is the limit for transmitter power on the 1.8 MHz band? 1500 watts PEP output.
lines.q: What is the limit for transmitter power on the 1.8 MHz band?
lines.a: 1500 watts PEP output.

lines.text: What must be done before using a new digital protocol on the air? Publicly document the technical characteristics of the protocol.
lines.q: What must be done before using a new digital protocol on the air?
lines.a: Publicly document the technical characteristics of the protocol.

lines.text: What measurement is specified by FCC rules that regulate maximum power? PEP output from the transmitter.
lines.q: What measurement is specified by FCC rules that regulate maximum power?
lines.a: PEP output from the transmitter.

lines.text: Group G1D.

Who may receive partial credit for the elements represented by an expired amateur radio license? Any person who can demonstrate that they once held an FCC-issued General, Advanced, or Amateur Extra class license that was not revoked by the FCC.
lines.q: Who may receive partial credit for the elements represented by an expired amateur radio license?
lines.a: Any person who can demonstrate that they once held an FCC-issued General, Advanced, or Amateur Extra class license that was not revoked by the FCC.

lines.text: What license examinations may you administer as an accredited Volunteer Examiner holding a General class operator license? Technician only.
lines.q: What license examinations may you administer as an accredited Volunteer Examiner holding a General class operator license?
lines.a: Technician only.

lines.text: On which of the following band segments may you operate if you are a Technician class operator and have an unexpired Certificate of Successful Completion of Examination (CSCE) for General class privileges? On any General or Technician class band segment.
lines.q: On which of the following band segments may you operate if you are a Technician class operator and have an unexpired Certificate of Successful Completion of Examination (CSCE) for General class privileges?
lines.a: On any General or Technician class band segment.

lines.text: Who must observe the administration of a Technician class license examination? At least three Volunteer Examiners of General class or higher.
lines.q: Who must observe the administration of a Technician class license examination?
lines.a: At least three Volunteer Examiners of General class or higher.

lines.text: When operating a US station by remote control from outside the country, what license is required of the control operator? A US operator/primary station license.
lines.q: When operating a US station by remote control from outside the country, what license is required of the control operator?
lines.a: A US operator/primary station license.

lines.text: Until an upgrade to General class is shown in the FCC database, when must a Technician licensee identify with “AG” after their call sign? Whenever they operate using General class frequency privileges.
lines.q: Until an upgrade to General class is shown in the FCC database, when must a Technician licensee identify with “AG” after their call sign?
lines.a: Whenever they operate using General class frequency privileges.

lines.text: Volunteer Examiners are accredited by what organization? A Volunteer Examiner Coordinator.
lines.q: Volunteer Examiners are accredited by what organization?
lines.a: A Volunteer Examiner Coordinator.

lines.text: Which of the following criteria must be met for a non-US citizen to be an accredited Volunteer Examiner? The person must hold an FCC granted amateur radio license of General class or above.
lines.q: Which of the following criteria must be met for a non-US citizen to be an accredited Volunteer Examiner?
lines.a: The person must hold an FCC granted amateur radio license of General class or above.

lines.text: How long is a Certificate of Successful Completion of Examination (CSCE) valid for exam element credit? 365 days.
lines.q: How long is a Certificate of Successful Completion of Examination (CSCE) valid for exam element credit?
lines.a: 365 days.

lines.text: What is the minimum age that one must be to qualify as an accredited Volunteer Examiner? 18 years.
lines.q: What is the minimum age that one must be to qualify as an accredited Volunteer Examiner?
lines.a: 18 years.

lines.text: What action is required to obtain a new General class license after a previously held license has expired and the two-year grace period has passed? The applicant must show proof of the appropriate expired license grant and pass the current Element 2 exam.
lines.q: What action is required to obtain a new General class license after a previously held license has expired and the two-year grace period has passed?
lines.a: The applicant must show proof of the appropriate expired license grant and pass the current Element 2 exam.

lines.text: When operating a station in South America by remote control over the internet from the US, what regulations apply? Only those of the remote station’s country.
lines.q: When operating a station in South America by remote control over the internet from the US, what regulations apply?
lines.a: Only those of the remote station’s country.

lines.text: Group G1E.
Which of the following would disqualify a third party from participating in sending a message via an amateur station? The third party’s amateur license has been revoked and not reinstated.
lines.q: Which of the following would disqualify a third party from participating in sending a message via an amateur station?
lines.a: The third party’s amateur license has been revoked and not reinstated.

lines.text: When may a 10-meter repeater retransmit the 2-meter signal from a station that has a Technician class control operator? Only if the 10-meter repeater control operator holds at least a General class license.
lines.q: When may a 10-meter repeater retransmit the 2-meter signal from a station that has a Technician class control operator?
lines.a: Only if the 10-meter repeater control operator holds at least a General class license.

lines.text: What is required to conduct communications with a digital station operating under automatic control outside the automatic control band segments? The station initiating the contact must be under local or remote control.
lines.q: What is required to conduct communications with a digital station operating under automatic control outside the automatic control band segments?
lines.a: The station initiating the contact must be under local or remote control.

lines.text: Which of the following conditions require a licensed amateur radio operator to take specific steps to avoid harmful interference to other users or facilities? When operating within one mile of an FCC Monitoring Station; When using a band where the Amateur Service is secondary; When a station is transmitting spread spectrum emissions; All these choices are correct.
lines.q: Which of the following conditions require a licensed amateur radio operator to take specific steps to avoid harmful interference to other users or facilities?
lines.a: When operating within one mile of an FCC Monitoring Station; When using a band where the Amateur Service is secondary; When a station is transmitting spread spectrum emissions; All these choices are correct.

lines.text: What are the restrictions on messages sent to a third party in a country with which there is a Third-Party Agreement? They must relate to amateur radio, or remarks of a personal character, or messages relating to emergencies or disaster relief.
lines.q: What are the restrictions on messages sent to a third party in a country with which there is a Third-Party Agreement?
lines.a: They must relate to amateur radio, or remarks of a personal character, or messages relating to emergencies or disaster relief.

lines.text: The frequency allocations of which ITU region apply to radio amateurs operating in North and South America? Region 2.
lines.q: The frequency allocations of which ITU region apply to radio amateurs operating in North and South America?
lines.a: Region 2.

lines.text: In what part of the 2.4 GHz band may an amateur station communicate with non-licensed Wi-Fi stations? No part.
lines.q: In what part of the 2.4 GHz band may an amateur station communicate with non-licensed Wi-Fi stations?
lines.a: No part.

lines.text: What is the maximum PEP output allowed for spread spectrum transmissions? 10 watts.
lines.q: What is the maximum PEP output allowed for spread spectrum transmissions?
lines.a: 10 watts.

lines.text: Why should an amateur operator normally avoid transmitting on 14.100, 18.110, 21.150, 24.930 and 28.200 MHz? A system of propagation beacon stations operates on those frequencies.
lines.q: Why should an amateur operator normally avoid transmitting on 14.100, 18.110, 21.150, 24.930 and 28.200 MHz?
lines.a: A system of propagation beacon stations operates on those frequencies.

lines.text: On what bands may automatically controlled stations transmitting RTTY or data emissions communicate with other automatically controlled digital stations? Anywhere in the 6-meter or shorter wavelength bands, and in limited segments of some of the HF bands.
lines.q: On what bands may automatically controlled stations transmitting RTTY or data emissions communicate with other automatically controlled digital stations?
lines.a: Anywhere in the 6-meter or shorter wavelength bands, and in limited segments of some of the HF bands.

lines.text: When may third-party messages be transmitted via remote control? Under any circumstances in which third party messages are permitted by FCC rules.
lines.q: When may third-party messages be transmitted via remote control?
lines.a: Under any circumstances in which third party messages are permitted by FCC rules.

lines.text: General answers. G2 - Operating Procedures.
Group G2A.
Which mode is most commonly used for voice communications on frequencies of 14 MHz or higher? Upper sideband.
lines.q: Which mode is most commonly used for voice communications on frequencies of 14 MHz or higher?
lines.a: Upper sideband.

lines.text: Which mode is most commonly used for voice communications on the 160-, 75-, and 40-meter bands? Lower sideband.
lines.q: Which mode is most commonly used for voice communications on the 160-, 75-, and 40-meter bands?
lines.a: Lower sideband.

lines.text: Which mode is most commonly used for SSB voice communications in the VHF and UHF bands? Upper sideband.
lines.q: Which mode is most commonly used for SSB voice communications in the VHF and UHF bands?
lines.a: Upper sideband.

lines.text: Which mode is most commonly used for voice communications on the 17- and 12-meter bands? Upper sideband.
lines.q: Which mode is most commonly used for voice communications on the 17- and 12-meter bands?
lines.a: Upper sideband.

lines.text: Which mode of voice communication is most commonly used on the HF amateur bands? Single sideband.
lines.q: Which mode of voice communication is most commonly used on the HF amateur bands?
lines.a: Single sideband.

lines.text: Which of the following is an advantage of using single sideband, as compared to other analog voice modes on the HF amateur bands? Less bandwidth used and greater power efficiency.
lines.q: Which of the following is an advantage of using single sideband, as compared to other analog voice modes on the HF amateur bands?
lines.a: Less bandwidth used and greater power efficiency.

lines.text: Which of the following statements is true of single sideband (SSB)? Only one sideband is transmitted; the other sideband and carrier are suppressed.
lines.q: Which of the following statements is true of single sideband (SSB)?
lines.a: Only one sideband is transmitted; the other sideband and carrier are suppressed.

lines.text: What is the recommended way to break into a phone contact? Say your call sign once.
lines.q: What is the recommended way to break into a phone contact?
lines.a: Say your call sign once.

lines.text: Why do most amateur stations use lower sideband on the 160-, 75-, and 40-meter bands? It is commonly accepted amateur practice.
lines.q: Why do most amateur stations use lower sideband on the 160-, 75-, and 40-meter bands?
lines.a: It is commonly accepted amateur practice.

lines.text: Which of the following statements is true of VOX operation versus PTT operation? It allows “hands free” operation.
lines.q: Which of the following statements is true of VOX operation versus PTT operation?
lines.a: It allows “hands free” operation.

lines.text: Generally, who should respond to a station in the contiguous 48 states calling “CQ DX”? Any stations outside the lower 48 states.
lines.q: Generally, who should respond to a station in the contiguous 48 states calling “CQ DX”?
lines.a: Any stations outside the lower 48 states.

lines.text: What control is typically adjusted for proper ALC setting on a single sideband transceiver? Transmit audio or microphone gain.
lines.q: What control is typically adjusted for proper ALC setting on a single sideband transceiver?
lines.a: Transmit audio or microphone gain.

lines.text: Group G2B.
Which of the following is true concerning access to frequencies? Except during emergencies, no amateur station has priority access to any frequency.
lines.q: Which of the following is true concerning access to frequencies?
lines.a: Except during emergencies, no amateur station has priority access to any frequency.

lines.text: What is the first thing you should do if you are communicating with another amateur station and hear a station in distress break in? Acknowledge the station in distress and determine what assistance may be needed.
lines.q: What is the first thing you should do if you are communicating with another amateur station and hear a station in distress break in?
lines.a: Acknowledge the station in distress and determine what assistance may be needed.

lines.text: What is good amateur practice if propagation changes during a contact creating interference from other stations using the frequency? Attempt to resolve the interference problem with the other stations in a mutually acceptable manner.
lines.q: What is good amateur practice if propagation changes during a contact creating interference from other stations using the frequency?
lines.a: Attempt to resolve the interference problem with the other stations in a mutually acceptable manner.

lines.text: When selecting a CW transmitting frequency, what minimum separation from other stations should be used to minimize interference to stations on adjacent frequencies? 150 Hz to 500 Hz.
lines.q: When selecting a CW transmitting frequency, what minimum separation from other stations should be used to minimize interference to stations on adjacent frequencies?
lines.a: 150 Hz to 500 Hz.

lines.text: When selecting an SSB transmitting frequency, what minimum separation should be used to minimize interference to stations on adjacent frequencies? 2 kHz to 3 kHz.
lines.q: When selecting an SSB transmitting frequency, what minimum separation should be used to minimize interference to stations on adjacent frequencies?
lines.a: 2 kHz to 3 kHz.

lines.text: How can you avoid harmful interference on an apparently clear frequency before calling CQ on CW or phone? Send “QRL?” on CW, followed by your call sign; or, if using phone, ask if the frequency is in use, followed by your call sign.
lines.q: How can you avoid harmful interference on an apparently clear frequency before calling CQ on CW or phone?
lines.a: Send “QRL?” on CW, followed by your call sign; or, if using phone, ask if the frequency is in use, followed by your call sign.

lines.text: Which of the following complies with commonly accepted amateur practice when choosing a frequency on which to initiate a call? Follow the voluntary band plan.
lines.q: Which of the following complies with commonly accepted amateur practice when choosing a frequency on which to initiate a call?
lines.a: Follow the voluntary band plan.

lines.text: What is the voluntary band plan restriction for US stations transmitting within the 48 contiguous states in the 50.1 MHz to 50.125 MHz band segment? Only contacts with stations not within the 48 contiguous states.
lines.q: What is the voluntary band plan restriction for US stations transmitting within the 48 contiguous states in the 50.1 MHz to 50.125 MHz band segment?
lines.a: Only contacts with stations not within the 48 contiguous states.

lines.text: Who may be the control operator of an amateur station transmitting in RACES to assist relief operations during a disaster? Only a person holding an FCC-issued amateur operator license.
lines.q: Who may be the control operator of an amateur station transmitting in RACES to assist relief operations during a disaster?
lines.a: Only a person holding an FCC-issued amateur operator license.

lines.text: Which of the following is good amateur practice for net management? Have a backup frequency in case of interference or poor conditions.
lines.q: Which of the following is good amateur practice for net management?
lines.a: Have a backup frequency in case of interference or poor conditions.

lines.text: How often may RACES training drills and tests be routinely conducted without special authorization? No more than 1 hour per week.
lines.q: How often may RACES training drills and tests be routinely conducted without special authorization?
lines.a: No more than 1 hour per week.

lines.text: Group G2C.
Which of the following describes full break-in CW operation (QSK)? Transmitting stations can receive between code characters and elements.
lines.q: Which of the following describes full break-in CW operation (QSK)?
lines.a: Transmitting stations can receive between code characters and elements.

lines.text: What should you do if a CW station sends “QRS?” Send slower.
lines.q: What should you do if a CW station sends “QRS?”
lines.a: Send slower.

lines.text: What does it mean when a CW operator sends “KN” at the end of a transmission? Listening only for a specific station or stations.
lines.q: What does it mean when a CW operator sends “KN” at the end of a transmission?
lines.a: Listening only for a specific station or stations.

lines.text: What does the Q signal “QRL?” mean? “Are you busy?” or “Is this frequency in use?”.
lines.q: What does the Q signal “QRL?” mean?
lines.a: “Are you busy?” or “Is this frequency in use?”.

lines.text: What is the best speed to use when answering a CQ in Morse code? The fastest speed at which you are comfortable copying, but no faster than the CQ.
lines.q: What is the best speed to use when answering a CQ in Morse code?
lines.a: The fastest speed at which you are comfortable copying, but no faster than the CQ.

lines.text: What does the term “zero beat” mean in CW operation? Matching the transmit frequency to the frequency of a received signal.
lines.q: What does the term “zero beat” mean in CW operation?
lines.a: Matching the transmit frequency to the frequency of a received signal.

lines.text: When sending CW, what does a “C” mean when added to the RST report? Chirpy or unstable signal.
lines.q: When sending CW, what does a “C” mean when added to the RST report?
lines.a: Chirpy or unstable signal.

lines.text: What prosign is sent to indicate the end of a formal message when using CW? AR.
lines.q: What prosign is sent to indicate the end of a formal message when using CW?
lines.a: AR.

lines.text: What does the Q signal “QSL” mean? I have received and understood.
lines.q: What does the Q signal “QSL” mean?
lines.a: I have received and understood.

lines.text: What does the Q signal “QRN” mean? I am troubled by static.
lines.q: What does the Q signal “QRN” mean?
lines.a: I am troubled by static.

lines.text: What does the Q signal “QRV” mean? I am ready to receive.
lines.q: What does the Q signal “QRV” mean?
lines.a: I am ready to receive.

lines.text: Group G2D.
What is the Volunteer Monitor Program? Amateur volunteers who are formally enlisted to monitor the airwaves for rules violations.
lines.q: What is the Volunteer Monitor Program?
lines.a: Amateur volunteers who are formally enlisted to monitor the airwaves for rules violations.

lines.text: Which of the following are objectives of the Volunteer Monitor Program? To encourage amateur radio operators to self-regulate and comply with the rules.
lines.q: Which of the following are objectives of the Volunteer Monitor Program?
lines.a: To encourage amateur radio operators to self-regulate and comply with the rules.

lines.text: What procedure may be used by Volunteer Monitors to localize a station whose continuous carrier is holding a repeater on in their area? Compare beam headings on the repeater input from their home locations with that of other Volunteer Monitors.
lines.q: What procedure may be used by Volunteer Monitors to localize a station whose continuous carrier is holding a repeater on in their area?
lines.a: Compare beam headings on the repeater input from their home locations with that of other Volunteer Monitors.

lines.text: Which of the following describes an azimuthal projection map? A map that shows true bearings and distances from a specific location.
lines.q: Which of the following describes an azimuthal projection map?
lines.a: A map that shows true bearings and distances from a specific location.

lines.text: Which of the following indicates that you are looking for an HF contact with any station? Repeat “CQ” a few times, followed by “this is,” then your call sign a few times, then pause to listen, repeat as necessary.
lines.q: Which of the following indicates that you are looking for an HF contact with any station?
lines.a: Repeat “CQ” a few times, followed by “this is,” then your call sign a few times, then pause to listen, repeat as necessary.

lines.text: How is a directional antenna pointed when making a “long-path” contact with another station? 180 degrees from the station’s short-path heading.
lines.q: How is a directional antenna pointed when making a “long-path” contact with another station?
lines.a: 180 degrees from the station’s short-path heading.

lines.text: Which of the following are examples of the NATO Phonetic Alphabet? Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, Delta.
lines.q: Which of the following are examples of the NATO Phonetic Alphabet?
lines.a: Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, Delta.

lines.text: Why do many amateurs keep a station log? To help with a reply if the FCC requests information about your station.
lines.q: Why do many amateurs keep a station log?
lines.a: To help with a reply if the FCC requests information about your station.

lines.text: Which of the following is required when participating in a contest on HF frequencies? Identify your station according to normal FCC regulations.
lines.q: Which of the following is required when participating in a contest on HF frequencies?
lines.a: Identify your station according to normal FCC regulations.

lines.text: What is QRP operation? Low-power transmit operation.
lines.q: What is QRP operation?
lines.a: Low-power transmit operation.

lines.text: Why are signal reports typically exchanged at the beginning of an HF contact? To allow each station to operate according to conditions.
lines.q: Why are signal reports typically exchanged at the beginning of an HF contact?
lines.a: To allow each station to operate according to conditions.

lines.text: Group G2E.
Which mode is normally used when sending RTTY signals via AFSK with an SSB transmitter? LSB.
lines.q: Which mode is normally used when sending RTTY signals via AFSK with an SSB transmitter?
lines.a: LSB.

lines.text: What is VARA? A digital protocol used with Winlink.
lines.q: What is VARA?
lines.a: A digital protocol used with Winlink.

lines.text: What symptoms may result from other signals interfering with a PACTOR or VARA transmission? Frequent retries or timeouts; Long pauses in message transmission; Failure to establish a connection between stations; All these choices are correct.
lines.q: What symptoms may result from other signals interfering with a PACTOR or VARA transmission?
lines.a: Frequent retries or timeouts; Long pauses in message transmission; Failure to establish a connection between stations; All these choices are correct.

lines.text: Which of the following is good practice when choosing a transmitting frequency to answer a station calling CQ using FT8? Find a clear frequency during the alternate time slot to the calling station.
lines.q: Which of the following is good practice when choosing a transmitting frequency to answer a station calling CQ using FT8?
lines.a: Find a clear frequency during the alternate time slot to the calling station.

lines.text: What is the standard sideband for JT65, JT9, FT4, or FT8 digital signal when using AFSK? USB.
lines.q: What is the standard sideband for JT65, JT9, FT4, or FT8 digital signal when using AFSK?
lines.a: USB.

lines.text: What is the most common frequency shift for RTTY emissions in the amateur HF bands? 170 Hz.
lines.q: What is the most common frequency shift for RTTY emissions in the amateur HF bands?

lines.text: Which of the following is required when using FT8? Computer time accurate to within approximately 1 second.
lines.q: Which of the following is required when using FT8?
lines.a: Computer time accurate to within approximately 1 second.

lines.text: In what segment of the 20-meter band are most digital mode operations commonly found? Between 14.070 MHz and 14.100 MHz.
lines.q: In what segment of the 20-meter band are most digital mode operations commonly found?
lines.a: Between 14.070 MHz and 14.100 MHz.

lines.text: How do you join a contact between two stations using the PACTOR protocol? Joining an existing contact is not possible, PACTOR connections are limited to two stations.
lines.q: How do you join a contact between two stations using the PACTOR protocol?
lines.a: Joining an existing contact is not possible, PACTOR connections are limited to two stations.

lines.text: Which of the following is a way to establish contact with a digital messaging system gateway station? Transmit a connect message on the station’s published frequency.
lines.q: Which of the following is a way to establish contact with a digital messaging system gateway station?
lines.a: Transmit a connect message on the station’s published frequency.

lines.text: What is the primary purpose of an Amateur Radio Emergency Data Network (AREDN) mesh network? To provide high-speed data services during an emergency or community event.
lines.q: What is the primary purpose of an Amateur Radio Emergency Data Network (AREDN) mesh network?
lines.a: To provide high-speed data services during an emergency or community event.

lines.text: Which of the following describes Winlink? An amateur radio wireless network to send and receive email on the internet; A form of Packet Radio; A wireless network capable of both VHF and HF band operation; All these choices are correct.
lines.q: Which of the following describes Winlink?
lines.a: An amateur radio wireless network to send and receive email on the internet; A form of Packet Radio; A wireless network capable of both VHF and HF band operation; All these choices are correct.

lines.text: What is another name for a Winlink Remote Message Server? Gateway.
lines.q: What is another name for a Winlink Remote Message Server?
lines.a: Gateway.

lines.text: What could be wrong if you cannot decode an RTTY or other FSK signal even though it is apparently tuned in properly? The mark and space frequencies may be reversed; You may have selected the wrong baud rate; You may be listening on the wrong sideband; All these choices are correct.
lines.q: What could be wrong if you cannot decode an RTTY or other FSK signal even though it is apparently tuned in properly?
lines.a: The mark and space frequencies may be reversed; You may have selected the wrong baud rate; You may be listening on the wrong sideband; All these choices are correct.

lines.text: Which of the following is a common location for FT8? Approximately 14.074 MHz to 14.077 MHz.
lines.q: Which of the following is a common location for FT8?
lines.a: Approximately 14.074 MHz to 14.077 MHz.

lines.text: General answers. G3 - Radio Wave Propagation.
Group G3A.
How does a higher sunspot number affect HF propagation? Higher sunspot numbers generally indicate a greater probability of good propagation at higher frequencies.
lines.q: How does a higher sunspot number affect HF propagation?
lines.a: Higher sunspot numbers generally indicate a greater probability of good propagation at higher frequencies.

lines.text: What effect does a sudden ionospheric disturbance have on the daytime ionospheric propagation? It disrupts signals on lower frequencies more than those on higher frequencies.
lines.q: What effect does a sudden ionospheric disturbance have on the daytime ionospheric propagation?
lines.a: It disrupts signals on lower frequencies more than those on higher frequencies.

lines.text: Approximately how long does it take the increased ultraviolet and X-ray radiation from a solar flare to affect radio propagation on Earth? 8 minutes.
lines.q: Approximately how long does it take the increased ultraviolet and X-ray radiation from a solar flare to affect radio propagation on Earth?
lines.a: 8 minutes.

lines.text: Which of the following are the least reliable bands for long-distance communications during periods of low solar activity? 15 meters, 12 meters, and 10 meters.
lines.q: Which of the following are the least reliable bands for long-distance communications during periods of low solar activity?
lines.a: 15 meters, 12 meters, and 10 meters.

lines.text: What is the solar flux index? A measure of solar radiation with a wavelength of 10.7 centimeters.
lines.q: What is the solar flux index?
lines.a: A measure of solar radiation with a wavelength of 10.7 centimeters.

lines.text: What is a geomagnetic storm? A temporary disturbance in Earth’s geomagnetic field.
lines.q: What is a geomagnetic storm?
lines.a: A temporary disturbance in Earth’s geomagnetic field.

lines.text: At what point in the solar cycle does the 20-meter band usually support worldwide propagation during daylight hours? At any point.
lines.q: At what point in the solar cycle does the 20-meter band usually support worldwide propagation during daylight hours?
lines.a: At any point.

lines.text: How can a geomagnetic storm affect HF propagation? Degrade high-latitude HF propagation.
lines.q: How can a geomagnetic storm affect HF propagation?
lines.a: Degrade high-latitude HF propagation.

lines.text: How can high geomagnetic activity benefit radio communications? Creates auroras that can reflect VHF signals.
lines.q: How can high geomagnetic activity benefit radio communications?
lines.a: Creates auroras that can reflect VHF signals.

lines.text: What causes HF propagation conditions to vary periodically in a 26- to 28-day cycle? Rotation of the Sun’s surface layers around its axis.
lines.q: What causes HF propagation conditions to vary periodically in a 26- to 28-day cycle?
lines.a: Rotation of the Sun’s surface layers around its axis.

lines.text: How long does it take a coronal mass ejection to affect radio propagation on Earth? 15 hours to several days.
lines.q: How long does it take a coronal mass ejection to affect radio propagation on Earth?
lines.a: 15 hours to several days.

lines.text: What does the K-index measure? The short-term stability of Earth’s geomagnetic field.
lines.q: What does the K-index measure?
lines.a: The short-term stability of Earth’s geomagnetic field.

lines.text: What does the A-index measure? The long-term stability of Earth’s geomagnetic field.
lines.q: What does the A-index measure?
lines.a: The long-term stability of Earth’s geomagnetic field.

lines.text: How is long distance radio communication usually affected by the charged particles that reach Earth from solar coronal holes? HF communication is disturbed.
lines.q: How is long distance radio communication usually affected by the charged particles that reach Earth from solar coronal holes?
lines.a: HF communication is disturbed.

lines.text: Group G3B.
What is a characteristic of skywave signals arriving at your location by both short-path and long-path propagation? A slightly delayed echo might be heard.
lines.q: What is a characteristic of skywave signals arriving at your location by both short-path and long-path propagation?
lines.a: A slightly delayed echo might be heard.

lines.text: What factors affect the MUF? Path distance and location; Time of day and season; Solar radiation and ionospheric disturbances; All these choices are correct.
lines.q: What factors affect the MUF?
lines.a: Path distance and location; Time of day and season; Solar radiation and ionospheric disturbances; All these choices are correct.

lines.text: Which frequency will have the least attenuation for long-distance skip propagation? Just below the MUF.
lines.q: Which frequency will have the least attenuation for long-distance skip propagation?
lines.a: Just below the MUF.

lines.text: Which of the following is a way to determine current propagation on a desired band from your station? Use a network of automated receiving stations on the internet to see where your transmissions are being received.
lines.q: Which of the following is a way to determine current propagation on a desired band from your station?
lines.a: Use a network of automated receiving stations on the internet to see where your transmissions are being received.

lines.text: How does the ionosphere affect radio waves with frequencies below the MUF and above the LUF? They are refracted back to Earth.
lines.q: How does the ionosphere affect radio waves with frequencies below the MUF and above the LUF?
lines.a: They are refracted back to Earth.

lines.text: What usually happens to radio waves with frequencies below the LUF? They are attenuated before reaching the destination.
lines.q: What usually happens to radio waves with frequencies below the LUF?
lines.a: They are attenuated before reaching the destination.

lines.text: What does LUF stand for? The Lowest Usable Frequency for communications between two specific points.
lines.q: What does LUF stand for?
lines.a: The Lowest Usable Frequency for communications between two specific points.

lines.text: What does MUF stand for? The Maximum Usable Frequency for communications between two points.
lines.q: What does MUF stand for?
lines.a: The Maximum Usable Frequency for communications between two points.

lines.text: What is the approximate maximum distance along the Earth’s surface normally covered in one hop using the F2 region? 2,500 miles.
lines.q: What is the approximate maximum distance along the Earth’s surface normally covered in one hop using the F2 region?
lines.a: 2,500 miles.

lines.text: What is the approximate maximum distance along the Earth’s surface normally covered in one hop using the E region? 1,200 miles.
lines.q: What is the approximate maximum distance along the Earth’s surface normally covered in one hop using the E region?
lines.a: 1,200 miles.

lines.text: What happens to HF propagation when the LUF exceeds the MUF? Propagation via ordinary skywave communications is not possible over that path.
lines.q: What happens to HF propagation when the LUF exceeds the MUF?
lines.a: Propagation via ordinary skywave communications is not possible over that path.

lines.text: Which of the following is typical of the lower HF frequencies during the summer? High levels of atmospheric noise or static.
lines.q: Which of the following is typical of the lower HF frequencies during the summer?
lines.a: High levels of atmospheric noise or static.

lines.text: Group G3C.
Which ionospheric region is closest to the surface of Earth? The D region.
lines.q: Which ionospheric region is closest to the surface of Earth?
lines.a: The D region.

lines.text: What is meant by the term “critical frequency” at a given incidence angle? The highest frequency which is refracted back to Earth.
lines.q: What is meant by the term “critical frequency” at a given incidence angle?
lines.a: The highest frequency which is refracted back to Earth.

lines.text: Why is skip propagation via the F2 region longer than that via the other ionospheric regions? Because it is the highest.
lines.q: Why is skip propagation via the F2 region longer than that via the other ionospheric regions?
lines.a: Because it is the highest.

lines.text: What does the term “critical angle” mean, as applied to radio wave propagation? The highest takeoff angle that will return a radio wave to Earth under specific ionospheric conditions.
lines.q: What does the term “critical angle” mean, as applied to radio wave propagation?
lines.a: The highest takeoff angle that will return a radio wave to Earth under specific ionospheric conditions.

lines.text: Why is long-distance communication on the 40-, 60-, 80-, and 160-meter bands more difficult during the day? The D region absorbs signals at these frequencies during daylight hours.
lines.q: Why is long-distance communication on the 40-, 60-, 80-, and 160-meter bands more difficult during the day?
lines.a: The D region absorbs signals at these frequencies during daylight hours.

lines.text: What is a characteristic of HF scatter? Signals have a fluttering sound.
lines.q: What is a characteristic of HF scatter?
lines.a: Signals have a fluttering sound.

lines.text: What makes HF scatter signals often sound distorted? Energy is scattered into the skip zone through several different paths.
lines.q: What makes HF scatter signals often sound distorted?
lines.a: Energy is scattered into the skip zone through several different paths.

lines.text: Why are HF scatter signals in the skip zone usually weak? Only a small part of the signal energy is scattered into the skip zone.
lines.q: Why are HF scatter signals in the skip zone usually weak?
lines.a: Only a small part of the signal energy is scattered into the skip zone.

lines.text: What type of propagation allows signals to be heard in the transmitting station’s skip zone? Scatter.
lines.q: What type of propagation allows signals to be heard in the transmitting station’s skip zone?
lines.a: Scatter.

lines.text: What is near vertical incidence skywave (NVIS) propagation? Short distance MF or HF propagation at high elevation angles.
lines.q: What is near vertical incidence skywave (NVIS) propagation?
lines.a: Short distance MF or HF propagation at high elevation angles.

lines.text: Which ionospheric region is the most absorbent of signals below 10 MHz during daylight hours? The D region.
lines.q: Which ionospheric region is the most absorbent of signals below 10 MHz during daylight hours?
lines.a: The D region.

lines.text: General answers. G4 - Amateur Radio Practices.
Group G4A.
What is the purpose of the notch filter found on many HF transceivers? To reduce interference from carriers in the receiver passband.
lines.q: What is the purpose of the notch filter found on many HF transceivers?
lines.a: To reduce interference from carriers in the receiver passband.

lines.text: What is the benefit of using the opposite or “reverse” sideband when receiving CW? It may be possible to reduce or eliminate interference from other signals.
lines.q: What is the benefit of using the opposite or “reverse” sideband when receiving CW?
lines.a: It may be possible to reduce or eliminate interference from other signals.

lines.text: How does a noise blanker work? By reducing receiver gain during a noise pulse.
lines.q: How does a noise blanker work?
lines.a: By reducing receiver gain during a noise pulse.

lines.text: What is the effect on plate current of the correct setting of a vacuum-tube RF power amplifier’s TUNE control? A pronounced dip.
lines.q: What is the effect on plate current of the correct setting of a vacuum-tube RF power amplifier’s TUNE control?
lines.a: A pronounced dip.

lines.text: Why is automatic level control (ALC) used with an RF power amplifier? To prevent excessive drive.
lines.q: Why is automatic level control (ALC) used with an RF power amplifier?
lines.a: To prevent excessive drive.

lines.text: What is the purpose of an antenna tuner? Increase power transfer from the transmitter to the feed line.
lines.q: What is the purpose of an antenna tuner?
lines.a: Increase power transfer from the transmitter to the feed line.

lines.text: What happens as a receiver’s noise reduction control level is increased? Received signals may become distorted.
lines.q: What happens as a receiver’s noise reduction control level is increased?
lines.a: Received signals may become distorted.

lines.text: What is the correct adjustment for the LOAD or COUPLING control of a vacuum tube RF power amplifier? Desired power output without exceeding maximum allowable plate current.
lines.q: What is the correct adjustment for the LOAD or COUPLING control of a vacuum tube RF power amplifier?
lines.a: Desired power output without exceeding maximum allowable plate current.

lines.text: What is the purpose of delaying RF output after activating a transmitter’s keying line to an external amplifier? To allow time for the amplifier to switch the antenna between the transceiver and the amplifier output.
lines.q: What is the purpose of delaying RF output after activating a transmitter’s keying line to an external amplifier?
lines.a: To allow time for the amplifier to switch the antenna between the transceiver and the amplifier output.

lines.text: What is the function of an electronic keyer? Automatic generation of dots and dashes for CW operation.
lines.q: What is the function of an electronic keyer?
lines.a: Automatic generation of dots and dashes for CW operation.

lines.text: Why should the ALC system be inactive when transmitting AFSK data signals? The ALC action distorts the signal.
lines.q: Why should the ALC system be inactive when transmitting AFSK data signals?
lines.a: The ALC action distorts the signal.

lines.text: Which of the following is a common use of the dual-VFO feature on a transceiver? To transmit on one frequency and listen on another.
lines.q: Which of the following is a common use of the dual-VFO feature on a transceiver?
lines.a: To transmit on one frequency and listen on another.

lines.text: What is the purpose of using a receive attenuator? To prevent receiver overload from strong incoming signals.
lines.q: What is the purpose of using a receive attenuator?
lines.a: To prevent receiver overload from strong incoming signals.

lines.text: Group G4B.
What item of test equipment contains horizontal and vertical channel amplifiers? An oscilloscope.
lines.q: What item of test equipment contains horizontal and vertical channel amplifiers?
lines.a: An oscilloscope.

lines.text: Which of the following is an advantage of an oscilloscope versus a digital voltmeter? Complex waveforms can be measured.
lines.q: Which of the following is an advantage of an oscilloscope versus a digital voltmeter?
lines.a: Complex waveforms can be measured.

lines.text: Which of the following is the best instrument to use for checking the keying waveform of a CW transmitter? An oscilloscope.
lines.q: Which of the following is the best instrument to use for checking the keying waveform of a CW transmitter?
lines.a: An oscilloscope.

lines.text: What signal source is connected to the vertical input of an oscilloscope when checking the RF envelope pattern of a transmitted signal? The attenuated RF output of the transmitter.
lines.q: What signal source is connected to the vertical input of an oscilloscope when checking the RF envelope pattern of a transmitted signal?
lines.a: The attenuated RF output of the transmitter.

lines.text: Why do voltmeters have high input impedance? It decreases the loading on circuits being measured.
lines.q: Why do voltmeters have high input impedance?
lines.a: It decreases the loading on circuits being measured.

lines.text: What is an advantage of a digital multimeter as compared to an analog multimeter? Higher precision.
lines.q: What is an advantage of a digital multimeter as compared to an analog multimeter?
lines.a: Higher precision.

lines.text: What signals are used to conduct a two-tone test? Two non-harmonically related audio signals.
lines.q: What signals are used to conduct a two-tone test?
lines.a: Two non-harmonically related audio signals.

lines.text: What transmitter performance parameter does a two-tone test analyze? Linearity.
lines.q: What transmitter performance parameter does a two-tone test analyze?
lines.a: Linearity.

lines.text: When is an analog multimeter preferred to a digital multimeter? When adjusting circuits for maximum or minimum values.
lines.q: When is an analog multimeter preferred to a digital multimeter?
lines.a: When adjusting circuits for maximum or minimum values.

lines.text: Which of the following can be determined with a directional wattmeter? Standing wave ratio.
lines.q: Which of the following can be determined with a directional wattmeter?
lines.a: Standing wave ratio.

lines.text: Which of the following must be connected to an antenna analyzer when it is being used for SWR measurements? Antenna and feed line.
lines.q: Which of the following must be connected to an antenna analyzer when it is being used for SWR measurements?
lines.a: Antenna and feed line.

lines.text: What effect can strong signals from nearby transmitters have on an antenna analyzer? Received power that interferes with SWR readings.
lines.q: What effect can strong signals from nearby transmitters have on an antenna analyzer?
lines.a: Received power that interferes with SWR readings.

lines.text: Which of the following can be measured with an antenna analyzer? Impedance of coaxial cable.
lines.q: Which of the following can be measured with an antenna analyzer?
lines.a: Impedance of coaxial cable.

lines.text: Group G4C.
Which of the following might be useful in reducing RF interference to audio frequency circuits? Bypass capacitor.
lines.q: Which of the following might be useful in reducing RF interference to audio frequency circuits?
lines.a: Bypass capacitor.

lines.text: Which of the following could be a cause of interference covering a wide range of frequencies? Arcing at a poor electrical connection.
lines.q: Which of the following could be a cause of interference covering a wide range of frequencies?
lines.a: Arcing at a poor electrical connection.

lines.text: What sound is heard from an audio device experiencing RF interference from a single sideband phone transmitter? Distorted speech.
lines.q: What sound is heard from an audio device experiencing RF interference from a single sideband phone transmitter?
lines.a: Distorted speech.

lines.text: What sound is heard from an audio device experiencing RF interference from a CW transmitter? On-and-off humming or clicking.
lines.q: What sound is heard from an audio device experiencing RF interference from a CW transmitter?
lines.a: On-and-off humming or clicking.

lines.text: What is a possible cause of high voltages that produce RF burns? The ground wire has high impedance on that frequency.
lines.q: What is a possible cause of high voltages that produce RF burns?
lines.a: The ground wire has high impedance on that frequency.

lines.text: What is a possible effect of a resonant ground connection? High RF voltages on the enclosures of station equipment.
lines.q: What is a possible effect of a resonant ground connection?
lines.a: High RF voltages on the enclosures of station equipment.

lines.text: Why should soldered joints not be used in lightning protection ground connections? A soldered joint will likely be destroyed by the heat of a lightning strike.
lines.q: Why should soldered joints not be used in lightning protection ground connections?
lines.a: A soldered joint will likely be destroyed by the heat of a lightning strike.

lines.text: What is the frequency above which a low-pass filter’s output power is less than half the input power? Cutoff frequency.

How is direct binary FSK modulation generated? By changing an oscillator’s frequency directly with a digital control signal.

lines.text: What is the name of the process that changes the phase angle of an RF signal to convey information? Phase modulation.

lines.text: What is the name of the process that changes the instantaneous frequency of an RF wave to convey information? Frequency modulation.

lines.a: Frequency modulation.

lines.text: What emission is produced by a reactance modulator connected to a transmitter RF amplifier stage? Phase modulation.
lines.q: What emission is produced by a reactance modulator connected to a transmitter RF amplifier stage?
lines.a: Phase modulation.

lines.text: What type of modulation varies the instantaneous power level of the RF signal? Amplitude modulation.
lines.q: What type of modulation varies the instantaneous power level of the RF signal?
lines.a: Amplitude modulation.

lines.text: Which of the following is characteristic of QPSK31? It is sideband sensitive; Its encoding provides error correction; Its bandwidth is approximately the same as BPSK31; All these choices are correct.

lines.text: Which of the following phone emissions uses the narrowest bandwidth? Single sideband.

lines.text: Which of the following is an effect of overmodulation? Excessive bandwidth.

lines.text: What type of modulation is used by FT8? 8-tone frequency shift keying.

lines.text: What is meant by the term “flat-topping,” when referring to an amplitude-modulated phone signal? Signal distortion caused by excessive drive or speech levels.

lines.a: Signal distortion caused by excessive drive or speech levels.

lines.text: What is the modulation envelope of an AM signal? The waveform created by connecting the peak values of the modulated signal.
lines.q: What is the modulation envelope of an AM signal?
lines.a: The waveform created by connecting the peak values of the modulated signal.

lines.text: What is QPSK modulation? Modulation in which digital data is transmitted using 0-, 90-, 180- and 270-degrees phase shift to represent pairs of bits.

lines.a: Modulation in which digital data is transmitted using 0-, 90-, 180- and 270-degrees phase shift to represent pairs of bits.

lines.text: What is a link budget? The sum of transmit power and antenna gains minus system losses as seen at the receiver.
lines.q: What is a link budget?

lines.text: What is link margin? The difference between received power level and minimum required signal level at the input to the receiver.
lines.q: What is link margin?
lines.a: The difference between received power level and minimum required signal level at the input to the receiver.

Which mixer input is varied or tuned to convert signals of different frequencies to an intermediate frequency (IF)? Local oscillator.

lines.text: What is the term for interference from a signal at twice the IF frequency from the desired signal? Image response.
lines.q: What is the term for interference from a signal at twice the IF frequency from the desired signal?

lines.text: What is another term for the mixing of two RF signals? Heterodyning.
lines.q: What is another term for the mixing of two RF signals?

lines.text: What is the stage in a VHF FM transmitter that generates a harmonic of a lower frequency signal to reach the desired operating frequency? Multiplier.

lines.text: Which intermodulation products are closest to the original signal frequencies? Odd-order.
lines.q: Which intermodulation products are closest to the original signal frequencies?

lines.a: Higher symbol rates require wider bandwidth.

lines.a: Intermodulation.

lines.q: Which digital mode is used as a low-power beacon for assessing HF propagation?

lines.text: What part of a packet radio frame contains the routing and handling information? Header.
lines.q: What part of a packet radio frame contains the routing and handling information?
lines.a: Header.

lines.text: Which of the following describes Baudot code? A 5-bit code with additional start and stop bits.
lines.q: Which of the following describes Baudot code?
lines.a: A 5-bit code with additional start and stop bits.

lines.text: In an ARQ mode, what is meant by a NAK response to a transmitted packet? Request retransmission of the packet.

lines.a: Request retransmission of the packet.

lines.text: Which of the following narrow-band digital modes can receive signals with very low signal-to-noise ratios? FT8.

lines.a: Upper case letters use longer Varicode bit sequences and thus slow down transmission.

lines.text: Which is true of mesh network microwave nodes? If one node fails, a packet may still reach its target station via an alternate node.
lines.q: Which is true of mesh network microwave nodes?
lines.a: If one node fails, a packet may still reach its target station via an alternate node.

lines.text: How does forward error correction (FEC) allow the receiver to correct data errors? By transmitting redundant information with the data.
lines.q: How does forward error correction (FEC) allow the receiver to correct data errors?
lines.a: By transmitting redundant information with the data.

lines.text: How are the two separate frequencies of a Frequency Shift Keyed (FSK) signal identified? Mark and space.
lines.q: How are the two separate frequencies of a Frequency Shift Keyed (FSK) signal identified?
lines.a: Mark and space.

lines.text: Which type of code is used for sending characters in a PSK31 signal? Varicode.
lines.q: Which type of code is used for sending characters in a PSK31 signal?
lines.a: Varicode.

lines.text: What is indicated on a waterfall display by one or more vertical lines on either side of a data mode or RTTY signal? Overmodulation.

lines.a: Overmodulation.

lines.text: Which of the following describes a waterfall display? Frequency is horizontal, signal strength is intensity, time is vertical.
lines.q: Which of the following describes a waterfall display?
lines.a: Frequency is horizontal, signal strength is intensity, time is vertical.

lines.q: What does an FT8 signal report of +3 mean?
lines.a: The signal-to-noise ratio is equivalent to +3dB in a 2.5 kHz bandwidth.

lines.text: Which of the following provide digital voice modes? DMR, D-STAR, and SystemFusion.
lines.q: Which of the following provide digital voice modes?
lines.a: DMR, D-STAR, and SystemFusion.

lines.text: General answers. G9 - Antennas and Feed Lines.
Group G9A.
Which of the following factors determine the characteristic impedance of a parallel conductor feed line? The distance between the centers of the conductors and the radius of the conductors.
lines.q: Which of the following factors determine the characteristic impedance of a parallel conductor feed line?
lines.a: The distance between the centers of the conductors and the radius of the conductors.

lines.text: What is the relationship between high standing wave ratio (SWR) and transmission line loss? High SWR increases loss in a lossy transmission line.
lines.q: What is the relationship between high standing wave ratio (SWR) and transmission line loss?
lines.a: High SWR increases loss in a lossy transmission line.

lines.text: What is the nominal characteristic impedance of “window line” transmission line? 450 ohms.
lines.q: What is the nominal characteristic impedance of “window line” transmission line?
lines.a: 450 ohms.

lines.text: What causes reflected power at an antenna’s feed point? A difference between feed line impedance and antenna feed point impedance.
lines.q: What causes reflected power at an antenna’s feed point?
lines.a: A difference between feed line impedance and antenna feed point impedance.

lines.text: How does the attenuation of coaxial cable change with increasing frequency? Attenuation increases.
lines.q: How does the attenuation of coaxial cable change with increasing frequency?
lines.a: Attenuation increases.

lines.text: In what units is RF feed line loss usually expressed? Decibels per 100 feet.
lines.q: In what units is RF feed line loss usually expressed?
lines.a: Decibels per 100 feet.

lines.text: What must be done to prevent standing waves on a feed line connected to an antenna? The antenna feed point impedance must be matched to the characteristic impedance of the feed line.
lines.q: What must be done to prevent standing waves on a feed line connected to an antenna?
lines.a: The antenna feed point impedance must be matched to the characteristic impedance of the feed line.

lines.text: If the SWR on an antenna feed line is 5:1, and a matching network at the transmitter end of the feed line is adjusted to present a 1:1 SWR to the transmitter, what is the resulting SWR on the feed line? 5:1.
