lines.text: What standing wave ratio results from connecting a 50-ohm feed line to a 200-ohm resistive load? 4:1.
lines.q: What standing wave ratio results from connecting a 50-ohm feed line to a 200-ohm resistive load?

lines.text: What standing wave ratio results from connecting a 50-ohm feed line to a 10-ohm resistive load? 5:1.
lines.q: What standing wave ratio results from connecting a 50-ohm feed line to a 10-ohm resistive load?

lines.text: What is the effect of transmission line loss on SWR measured at the input to the line? Higher loss reduces SWR measured at the input to the line.
lines.q: What is the effect of transmission line loss on SWR measured at the input to the line?
lines.a: Higher loss reduces SWR measured at the input to the line.

lines.text: Group G9B.
What is a characteristic of a random-wire HF antenna connected directly to the transmitter? Station equipment may carry significant RF current.
lines.q: What is a characteristic of a random-wire HF antenna connected directly to the transmitter?
lines.a: Station equipment may carry significant RF current.

lines.text: Which of the following is a common way to adjust the feed point impedance of an elevated quarter-wave ground-plane vertical antenna to be approximately 50 ohms? Slope the radials downward.
lines.q: Which of the following is a common way to adjust the feed point impedance of an elevated quarter-wave ground-plane vertical antenna to be approximately 50 ohms?
lines.a: Slope the radials downward.

lines.text: Which of the following best describes the radiation pattern of a quarter-wave ground-plane vertical antenna? Omnidirectional in azimuth.
lines.q: Which of the following best describes the radiation pattern of a quarter-wave ground-plane vertical antenna?
lines.a: Omnidirectional in azimuth.

lines.text: What is the radiation pattern of a dipole antenna in free space in a plane containing the conductor? It is a figure-eight at right angles to the antenna.
lines.q: What is the radiation pattern of a dipole antenna in free space in a plane containing the conductor?
lines.a: It is a figure-eight at right angles to the antenna.

lines.text: How does antenna height affect the azimuthal radiation pattern of a horizontal dipole HF antenna at elevation angles higher than about 45 degrees? If the antenna is less than 1/2 wavelength high, the azimuthal pattern is almost omnidirectional.
lines.q: How does antenna height affect the azimuthal radiation pattern of a horizontal dipole HF antenna at elevation angles higher than about 45 degrees?
lines.a: If the antenna is less than 1/2 wavelength high, the azimuthal pattern is almost omnidirectional.

lines.text: Where should the radial wires of a ground-mounted vertical antenna system be placed? On the surface or buried a few inches below the ground.
lines.q: Where should the radial wires of a ground-mounted vertical antenna system be placed?
lines.a: On the surface or buried a few inches below the ground.

lines.text: How does the feed point impedance of a horizontal 1/2 wave dipole antenna change as the antenna height is reduced to 1/10 wavelength above ground? It steadily decreases.
lines.q: How does the feed point impedance of a horizontal 1/2 wave dipole antenna change as the antenna height is reduced to 1/10 wavelength above ground?
lines.a: It steadily decreases.

lines.text: How does the feed point impedance of a 1/2 wave dipole change as the feed point is moved from the center toward the ends? It steadily increases.
lines.q: How does the feed point impedance of a 1/2 wave dipole change as the feed point is moved from the center toward the ends?
lines.a: It steadily increases.

lines.text: Which of the following is an advantage of using a horizontally polarized as compared to a vertically polarized HF antenna? Lower ground losses.
lines.q: Which of the following is an advantage of using a horizontally polarized as compared to a vertically polarized HF antenna?
lines.a: Lower ground losses.

lines.text: What is the approximate length for a 1/2 wave dipole antenna cut for 14.250 MHz? 33 feet.
lines.q: What is the approximate length for a 1/2 wave dipole antenna cut for 14.250 MHz?
lines.a: 33 feet.

lines.text: What is the approximate length for a 1/2 wave dipole antenna cut for 3.550 MHz? 132 feet.
lines.q: What is the approximate length for a 1/2 wave dipole antenna cut for 3.550 MHz?
lines.a: 132 feet.

lines.text: What is the approximate length for a 1/4 wave monopole antenna cut for 28.5 MHz? 8 feet.
lines.q: What is the approximate length for a 1/4 wave monopole antenna cut for 28.5 MHz?
lines.a: 8 feet.

lines.text: Group G9C.
Which of the following would increase the bandwidth of a Yagi antenna? Larger-diameter elements.
lines.q: Which of the following would increase the bandwidth of a Yagi antenna?
lines.a: Larger-diameter elements.

lines.text: What is the approximate length of the driven element of a Yagi antenna? 1/2 wavelength.
lines.q: What is the approximate length of the driven element of a Yagi antenna?
lines.a: 1/2 wavelength.

lines.text: How do the lengths of a three-element Yagi reflector and director compare to that of the driven element? The reflector is longer, and the director is shorter.
lines.q: How do the lengths of a three-element Yagi reflector and director compare to that of the driven element?
lines.a: The reflector is longer, and the director is shorter.

lines.text: How does antenna gain in dBi compare to gain stated in dBd for the same antenna? Gain in dBi is 2.15 dB higher.
lines.q: How does antenna gain in dBi compare to gain stated in dBd for the same antenna?
lines.a: Gain in dBi is 2.15 dB higher.

lines.text: What is the primary effect of increasing boom length and adding directors to a Yagi antenna? Gain increases.
lines.q: What is the primary effect of increasing boom length and adding directors to a Yagi antenna?
lines.a: Gain increases.

lines.text: What does “front-to-back ratio” mean in reference to a Yagi antenna? The power radiated in the major lobe compared to that in the opposite direction.
lines.q: What does “front-to-back ratio” mean in reference to a Yagi antenna?
lines.a: The power radiated in the major lobe compared to that in the opposite direction.

lines.text: What is meant by the “main lobe” of a directive antenna? The direction of maximum radiated field strength from the antenna.
lines.q: What is meant by the “main lobe” of a directive antenna?
lines.a: The direction of maximum radiated field strength from the antenna.

lines.text: In free space, how does the gain of two three-element, horizontally polarized Yagi antennas spaced vertically 1/2 wavelength apart typically compare to the gain of a single three-element Yagi? Approximately 3 dB higher.
lines.q: In free space, how does the gain of two three-element, horizontally polarized Yagi antennas spaced vertically 1/2 wavelength apart typically compare to the gain of a single three-element Yagi?
lines.a: Approximately 3 dB higher.

lines.text: Which of the following can be adjusted to optimize forward gain, front-to-back ratio, or SWR bandwidth of a Yagi antenna? The physical length of the boom; The number of elements on the boom; The spacing of each element along the boom; All these choices are correct.

lines.a: The physical length of the boom; The number of elements on the boom; The spacing of each element along the boom; All these choices are correct.

lines.text: What is a beta or hairpin match? A shorted transmission line stub placed at the feed point of a Yagi antenna to provide impedance matching.
lines.q: What is a beta or hairpin match?
lines.a: A shorted transmission line stub placed at the feed point of a Yagi antenna to provide impedance matching.

lines.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of using a gamma match with a Yagi antenna? It does not require the driven element to be insulated from the boom.
lines.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of using a gamma match with a Yagi antenna?
lines.a: It does not require the driven element to be insulated from the boom.

lines.text: What is the feed point impedance of an end-fed half-wave antenna? Very high.

lines.a: Omnidirectional in the plane of the halo.

lines.text: What is an advantage of vertically stacking horizontally polarized Yagi antennas? It narrows the main lobe in elevation.

lines.a: It narrows the main lobe in elevation.

lines.text: Which of the following is an advantage of a log-periodic antenna? Wide bandwidth.

lines.text: How does a “screwdriver” mobile antenna adjust its feed point impedance? By varying the base loading inductance.
lines.q: How does a “screwdriver” mobile antenna adjust its feed point impedance?
lines.a: By varying the base loading inductance.

lines.text: What is the primary use of a Beverage antenna? Directional receiving for MF and low HF bands.
lines.q: What is the primary use of a Beverage antenna?
lines.a: Directional receiving for MF and low HF bands.

lines.text: In which direction or directions does an electrically small loop (less than 1/10 wavelength in circumference) have nulls in its radiation pattern? Broadside to the loop.
lines.q: In which direction or directions does an electrically small loop (less than 1/10 wavelength in circumference) have nulls in its radiation pattern?

lines.text: Which of the following is a disadvantage of multiband antennas? They have poor harmonic rejection.
lines.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of multiband antennas?
lines.a: They have poor harmonic rejection.

lines.text: What is the common name of a dipole with a single central support? Inverted V.
lines.q: What is the common name of a dipole with a single central support?

lines.text: General answers. G0 - Electrical and RF Safety.
Group G0A.
What is one way that RF energy can affect human body tissue? It heats body tissue.
lines.q: What is one way that RF energy can affect human body tissue?
lines.a: It heats body tissue.

lines.text: Which of the following is used to determine RF exposure from a transmitted signal? Its duty cycle; Its frequency; Its power density; All these choices are correct.
lines.q: Which of the following is used to determine RF exposure from a transmitted signal?
lines.a: Its duty cycle; Its frequency; Its power density; All these choices are correct.

lines.text: How can you determine that your station complies with FCC RF exposure regulations? By calculation based on FCC OET Bulletin 65; By calculation based on computer modeling; By measurement of field strength using calibrated equipment; All these choices are correct.
lines.q: How can you determine that your station complies with FCC RF exposure regulations?
lines.a: By calculation based on FCC OET Bulletin 65; By calculation based on computer modeling; By measurement of field strength using calibrated equipment; All these choices are correct.

lines.text: What does “time averaging” mean when evaluating RF radiation exposure? The total RF exposure averaged over a certain period.
lines.q: What does “time averaging” mean when evaluating RF radiation exposure?
lines.a: The total RF exposure averaged over a certain period.

lines.text: What must you do if an evaluation of your station shows that the RF energy radiated by your station exceeds permissible limits for possible human absorption? Take action to prevent human exposure to the excessive RF fields.
lines.q: What must you do if an evaluation of your station shows that the RF energy radiated by your station exceeds permissible limits for possible human absorption?
lines.a: Take action to prevent human exposure to the excessive RF fields.

lines.text: What must you do if your station fails to meet the FCC RF exposure exemption criteria? Perform an RF exposure evaluation in accordance with FCC OET Bulletin 65.

lines.a: Perform an RF exposure evaluation in accordance with FCC OET Bulletin 65.

lines.text: What is the effect of modulation duty cycle on RF exposure? A lower duty cycle permits greater power levels to be transmitted.
lines.q: What is the effect of modulation duty cycle on RF exposure?
lines.a: A lower duty cycle permits greater power levels to be transmitted.

lines.text: Which of the following steps must an amateur operator take to ensure compliance with RF safety regulations? Perform a routine RF exposure evaluation and prevent access to any identified high exposure areas.
lines.q: Which of the following steps must an amateur operator take to ensure compliance with RF safety regulations?
lines.a: Perform a routine RF exposure evaluation and prevent access to any identified high exposure areas.

lines.text: What type of instrument can be used to accurately measure an RF field strength? A calibrated field strength meter with a calibrated antenna.
lines.q: What type of instrument can be used to accurately measure an RF field strength?

lines.text: What should be done if evaluation shows that a neighbor might experience more than the allowable limit of RF exposure from the main lobe of a directional antenna? Take precautions to ensure that the antenna cannot be pointed in their direction when they are present.

lines.text: What precaution should be taken if you install an indoor transmitting antenna? Make sure that MPE limits are not exceeded in occupied areas.

lines.a: Make sure that MPE limits are not exceeded in occupied areas.

lines.text: What stations are subject to the FCC rules on RF exposure? All stations with a time-averaged transmission of more than one milliwatt.

lines.a: All stations with a time-averaged transmission of more than one milliwatt.

lines.text: Which of the following is a danger from lead-tin solder? Lead can contaminate food if hands are not washed carefully after handling the solder.

lines.a: Lead can contaminate food if hands are not washed carefully after handling the solder.

lines.text: Which of the following is required for lightning protection ground rods? They must be bonded together with all other grounds.

lines.text: What is the purpose of a power supply interlock? To ensure that dangerous voltages are removed if the cabinet is opened.

lines.a: To ensure that dangerous voltages are removed if the cabinet is opened.

lines.text: Where should lightning arrestors be located? Where the feed lines enter the building.

lines.a: Where the feed lines enter the building.

Why is it not legal to transmit a 3 kHz bandwidth USB signal with a carrier frequency of 14.348 MHz? The upper 1 kHz of the signal is outside the 20-meter band.

lines.a: The upper 1 kHz of the signal is outside the 20-meter band.

lines.text: When using a transceiver that displays the carrier frequency of phone signals, which of the following displayed frequencies represents the lowest frequency at which a properly adjusted LSB emission will be totally within the band? 3 kHz above the lower band edge.
lines.q: When using a transceiver that displays the carrier frequency of phone signals, which of the following displayed frequencies represents the lowest frequency at which a properly adjusted LSB emission will be totally within the band?
lines.a: 3 kHz above the lower band edge.

lines.text: What is the highest legal carrier frequency on the 20-meter band for transmitting a 2.8 kHz wide USB data signal? 14.1472 MHz.

lines.text: May an Extra class operator answer the CQ of a station on 3.601 MHz LSB phone? No, the sideband components will extend beyond the edge of the phone band segment.

lines.a: No, the sideband components will extend beyond the edge of the phone band segment.

lines.text: Who must be in physical control of the station apparatus of an amateur station aboard any vessel or craft that is documented or registered in the United States? Any person holding an FCC issued amateur license or who is authorized for alien reciprocal operation.
lines.q: Who must be in physical control of the station apparatus of an amateur station aboard any vessel or craft that is documented or registered in the United States?
lines.a: Any person holding an FCC issued amateur license or who is authorized for alien reciprocal operation.

lines.text: What is the required transmit frequency of a CW signal for channelized 60 meter operation? At the center frequency of the channel.
lines.q: What is the required transmit frequency of a CW signal for channelized 60 meter operation?
lines.a: At the center frequency of the channel.

lines.text: What is the maximum power permitted on the 2200-meter band? 1 watt EIRP (equivalent isotropic radiated power).
lines.q: What is the maximum power permitted on the 2200-meter band?
lines.a: 1 watt EIRP (equivalent isotropic radiated power).

lines.text: If a station in a message forwarding system inadvertently forwards a message that is in violation of FCC rules, who is primarily accountable for the rules violation? The control operator of the originating station.
lines.q: If a station in a message forwarding system inadvertently forwards a message that is in violation of FCC rules, who is primarily accountable for the rules violation?
lines.a: The control operator of the originating station.

lines.text: Except in some parts of Alaska, what is the maximum power permitted on the 630-meter band? 5 watts EIRP (equivalent isotropic radiated power).
lines.q: Except in some parts of Alaska, what is the maximum power permitted on the 630-meter band?
lines.a: 5 watts EIRP (equivalent isotropic radiated power).

lines.text: If an amateur station is installed aboard a ship or aircraft, what condition must be met before the station is operated? Its operation must be approved by the master of the ship or the pilot in command of the aircraft.
lines.q: If an amateur station is installed aboard a ship or aircraft, what condition must be met before the station is operated?
lines.a: Its operation must be approved by the master of the ship or the pilot in command of the aircraft.

lines.text: What licensing is required when operating an amateur station aboard a US-registered vessel in international waters? Any FCC-issued amateur license.
lines.q: What licensing is required when operating an amateur station aboard a US-registered vessel in international waters?
lines.a: Any FCC-issued amateur license.

lines.text: Group E1B.
Which of the following constitutes a spurious emission? An emission outside the signal’s necessary bandwidth that can be reduced or eliminated without affecting the information transmitted.
lines.q: Which of the following constitutes a spurious emission?
lines.a: An emission outside the signal’s necessary bandwidth that can be reduced or eliminated without affecting the information transmitted.

lines.text: Which of the following is an acceptable bandwidth for digital voice or slow-scan TV transmissions made on the HF amateur bands? 3 kHz.
lines.q: Which of the following is an acceptable bandwidth for digital voice or slow-scan TV transmissions made on the HF amateur bands?
lines.a: 3 kHz.

lines.text: Within what distance must an amateur station protect an FCC monitoring facility from harmful interference? 1 mile.
lines.q: Within what distance must an amateur station protect an FCC monitoring facility from harmful interference?
lines.a: 1 mile.

lines.q: What must the control operator of a repeater operating in the 70-centimeter band do if a radiolocation system experiences interference from that repeater?
lines.a: Cease operation or make changes to the repeater that mitigate the interference.

lines.text: What is the National Radio Quiet Zone? An area surrounding the National Radio Astronomy Observatory.
lines.q: What is the National Radio Quiet Zone?
lines.a: An area surrounding the National Radio Astronomy Observatory.

lines.text: Which of the following additional rules apply if you are erecting an amateur station antenna structure at a site at or near a public use airport? You may have to notify the Federal Aviation Administration and register it with the FCC as required by Part 17 of the FCC rules.
lines.q: Which of the following additional rules apply if you are erecting an amateur station antenna structure at a site at or near a public use airport?
lines.a: You may have to notify the Federal Aviation Administration and register it with the FCC as required by Part 17 of the FCC rules.

lines.text: To what type of regulations does PRB-1 apply? State and local zoning.
lines.q: To what type of regulations does PRB-1 apply?
lines.a: State and local zoning.

lines.text: What limitations may the FCC place on an amateur station if its signal causes interference to domestic broadcast reception, assuming that the receivers involved are of good engineering design? The amateur station must avoid transmitting during certain hours on frequencies that cause the interference.
lines.q: What limitations may the FCC place on an amateur station if its signal causes interference to domestic broadcast reception, assuming that the receivers involved are of good engineering design?
lines.a: The amateur station must avoid transmitting during certain hours on frequencies that cause the interference.

lines.text: Which amateur stations may be operated under RACES rules? Any FCC-licensed amateur station certified by the responsible civil defense organization for the area served.
lines.q: Which amateur stations may be operated under RACES rules?
lines.a: Any FCC-licensed amateur station certified by the responsible civil defense organization for the area served.

lines.text: What frequencies are authorized to an amateur station operating under RACES rules? All amateur service frequencies authorized to the control operator.
lines.q: What frequencies are authorized to an amateur station operating under RACES rules?
lines.a: All amateur service frequencies authorized to the control operator.

lines.text: What does PRB-1 require of state and local regulations affecting amateur radio antenna size and structures? Reasonable accommodations of amateur radio must be made.
lines.q: What does PRB-1 require of state and local regulations affecting amateur radio antenna size and structures?
lines.a: Reasonable accommodations of amateur radio must be made.

lines.text: Group E1C.
What is the maximum bandwidth for a data emission on 60 meters? 2.8 kHz.
lines.q: What is the maximum bandwidth for a data emission on 60 meters?
lines.a: 2.8 kHz.

lines.text: Which of the following apply to communications transmitted to amateur stations in foreign countries? Communications must be limited to those incidental to the purpose of the amateur service and remarks of a personal nature.
lines.q: Which of the following apply to communications transmitted to amateur stations in foreign countries?
lines.a: Communications must be limited to those incidental to the purpose of the amateur service and remarks of a personal nature.

lines.text: How long must an operator wait after filing a notification with the Utilities Technology Council (UTC) before operating on the 2200-meter or 630-meter band? lines.q: How long must an operator wait after filing a notification with the Utilities Technology Council (UTC) before operating on the 2200-meter or 630-meter band?
lines.a: Operators may operate after 30 days, providing they have not been told that their station is within 1 kilometer of PLC systems using those frequencies.

lines.text: What is an IARP? A permit that allows US amateurs to operate in certain countries of the Americas.
lines.q: What is an IARP?
lines.a: A permit that allows US amateurs to operate in certain countries of the Americas.

lines.text: Under what situation may a station transmit third party communications while being automatically controlled? Only when transmitting RTTY or data emissions.
lines.q: Under what situation may a station transmit third party communications while being automatically controlled?
lines.a: Only when transmitting RTTY or data emissions.

lines.text: Which of the following is required in order to operate in accordance with CEPT rules in foreign countries where permitted? You must have a copy of FCC Public Notice DA 16-1048.
lines.q: Which of the following is required in order to operate in accordance with CEPT rules in foreign countries where permitted?
lines.a: You must have a copy of FCC Public Notice DA 16-1048.

lines.text: What notifications must be given before transmitting on the 630- or 2200-meter bands? Operators must inform the Utilities Technology Council (UTC) of their call sign and coordinates of the station.
lines.q: What notifications must be given before transmitting on the 630- or 2200-meter bands?
lines.a: Operators must inform the Utilities Technology Council (UTC) of their call sign and coordinates of the station.

lines.text: What is the maximum permissible duration of a remotely controlled station’s transmissions if its control link malfunctions? 3 minutes.
lines.q: What is the maximum permissible duration of a remotely controlled station’s transmissions if its control link malfunctions?
lines.a: 3 minutes.

lines.text: What is the highest modulation index permitted at the highest modulation frequency for angle modulation below 29.0 MHz? 1.0.
lines.q: What is the highest modulation index permitted at the highest modulation frequency for angle modulation below 29.0 MHz?

lines.text: What is the maximum mean power level for a spurious emission below 30 MHz with respect to the fundamental emission? - 43 dB.
lines.q: What is the maximum mean power level for a spurious emission below 30 MHz with respect to the fundamental emission?

lines.text: Which of the following operating arrangements allows an FCC-licensed US citizen to operate in many European countries, and amateurs from many European countries to operate in the US? CEPT.
lines.q: Which of the following operating arrangements allows an FCC-licensed US citizen to operate in many European countries, and amateurs from many European countries to operate in the US?
lines.a: CEPT.

lines.text: In what portion of the 630-meter band are phone emissions permitted? The entire band.
lines.q: In what portion of the 630-meter band are phone emissions permitted?
lines.a: The entire band.

lines.text: Group E1D.
What is the definition of telemetry? One-way transmission of measurements at a distance from the measuring instrument.
lines.q: What is the definition of telemetry?
lines.a: One-way transmission of measurements at a distance from the measuring instrument.

lines.text: Which of the following may transmit encrypted messages? Telecommand signals from a space telecommand station.
lines.q: Which of the following may transmit encrypted messages?
lines.a: Telecommand signals from a space telecommand station.

lines.text: What is a space telecommand station? An amateur station that transmits communications to initiate, modify, or terminate functions of a space station.
lines.q: What is a space telecommand station?
lines.a: An amateur station that transmits communications to initiate, modify, or terminate functions of a space station.

lines.text: Which of the following is required in the identification transmissions from a balloon-borne telemetry station? Call sign.
lines.q: Which of the following is required in the identification transmissions from a balloon-borne telemetry station?
lines.a: Call sign.

lines.text: What must be posted at the location of a station being operated by telecommand on or within 50 kilometers of the Earth’s surface? A photocopy of the station license; A label with the name, address, and telephone number of the station licensee; A label with the name, address, and telephone number of the control operator; All these choices are correct.
lines.q: What must be posted at the location of a station being operated by telecommand on or within 50 kilometers of the Earth’s surface?
lines.a: A photocopy of the station license; A label with the name, address, and telephone number of the station licensee; A label with the name, address, and telephone number of the control operator; All these choices are correct.

lines.text: What is the maximum permitted transmitter output power when operating a model craft by telecommand? 1 watt.
lines.q: What is the maximum permitted transmitter output power when operating a model craft by telecommand?
lines.a: 1 watt.

lines.text: Which of the following HF amateur bands include allocations for space stations? 40 meters, 20 meters, 15 meters, and 10 meters.
lines.q: Which of the following HF amateur bands include allocations for space stations?
lines.a: 40 meters, 20 meters, 15 meters, and 10 meters.

lines.text: Which VHF amateur bands have frequencies authorized for space stations? 2 meters.
lines.q: Which VHF amateur bands have frequencies authorized for space stations?
lines.a: 2 meters.

lines.text: Which UHF amateur bands have frequencies authorized for space stations? 70 centimeters and 13 centimeters.
lines.q: Which UHF amateur bands have frequencies authorized for space stations?
lines.a: 70 centimeters and 13 centimeters.

lines.text: Which amateur stations are eligible to be telecommand stations of space stations, subject to the privileges of the class of operator license held by the control operator of the station? Any amateur station so designated by the space station licensee.
lines.q: Which amateur stations are eligible to be telecommand stations of space stations, subject to the privileges of the class of operator license held by the control operator of the station?
lines.a: Any amateur station so designated by the space station licensee.

lines.text: Which amateur stations are eligible to operate as Earth stations? Any amateur station, subject to the privileges of the class of operator license held by the control operator.
lines.q: Which amateur stations are eligible to operate as Earth stations?
lines.a: Any amateur station, subject to the privileges of the class of operator license held by the control operator.

lines.text: Which of the following amateur stations may transmit one-way communications? A space station, beacon station, or telecommand station.
lines.q: Which of the following amateur stations may transmit one-way communications?
lines.a: A space station, beacon station, or telecommand station.

lines.text: Group E1E.

For which types of out-of-pocket expenses do the Part 97 rules state that VEs and VECs may be reimbursed? Preparing, processing, administering, and coordinating an examination for an amateur radio operator license.
lines.q: For which types of out-of-pocket expenses do the Part 97 rules state that VEs and VECs may be reimbursed?
lines.a: Preparing, processing, administering, and coordinating an examination for an amateur radio operator license.

lines.text: Who is tasked by Part 97 with maintaining the pools of questions for all US amateur license examinations? The VECs.
lines.q: Who is tasked by Part 97 with maintaining the pools of questions for all US amateur license examinations?
lines.a: The VECs.

lines.text: What is a Volunteer Examiner Coordinator? An organization that has entered into an agreement with the FCC to coordinate, prepare, and administer amateur operator license examinations.
lines.q: What is a Volunteer Examiner Coordinator?
lines.a: An organization that has entered into an agreement with the FCC to coordinate, prepare, and administer amateur operator license examinations.

lines.text: What is required to be accredited as a Volunteer Examiner? A VEC must confirm that the VE applicant meets FCC requirements to serve as an examiner.
lines.q: What is required to be accredited as a Volunteer Examiner?
lines.a: A VEC must confirm that the VE applicant meets FCC requirements to serve as an examiner.

lines.text: What must the VE team do with the application form if the examinee does not pass the exam? Return the application document to the examinee.
lines.q: What must the VE team do with the application form if the examinee does not pass the exam?
lines.a: Return the application document to the examinee.

lines.text: Who is responsible for the proper conduct and necessary supervision during an amateur operator license examination session? Each administering VE.
lines.q: Who is responsible for the proper conduct and necessary supervision during an amateur operator license examination session?
lines.a: Each administering VE.

lines.text: What should a VE do if a candidate fails to comply with the examiner’s instructions during an amateur operator license examination? Immediately terminate the candidate’s examination.
lines.q: What should a VE do if a candidate fails to comply with the examiner’s instructions during an amateur operator license examination?
lines.a: Immediately terminate the candidate’s examination.

lines.text: To which of the following examinees may a VE not administer an examination? Relatives of the VE as listed in the FCC rules.
lines.q: To which of the following examinees may a VE not administer an examination?
lines.a: Relatives of the VE as listed in the FCC rules.

lines.text: What may be the penalty for a VE who fraudulently administers or certifies an examination? Revocation of the VE’s amateur station license grant and the suspension of the VE’s amateur operator license grant.
lines.q: What may be the penalty for a VE who fraudulently administers or certifies an examination?
lines.a: Revocation of the VE’s amateur station license grant and the suspension of the VE’s amateur operator license grant.

lines.text: What must the administering VEs do after the administration of a successful examination for an amateur operator license? They must submit the application document to the coordinating VEC according to the coordinating VEC instructions.
lines.q: What must the administering VEs do after the administration of a successful examination for an amateur operator license?
lines.a: They must submit the application document to the coordinating VEC according to the coordinating VEC instructions.

lines.text: What must the VE team do if an examinee scores a passing grade on all examination elements needed for an upgrade or new license? Three VEs must certify that the examinee is qualified for the license grant and that they have complied with the administering VE requirements.
lines.q: What must the VE team do if an examinee scores a passing grade on all examination elements needed for an upgrade or new license?
lines.a: Three VEs must certify that the examinee is qualified for the license grant and that they have complied with the administering VE requirements.

lines.text: Group E1F.
On what frequencies are spread spectrum transmissions permitted? Only on amateur frequencies above 222 MHz.
lines.q: On what frequencies are spread spectrum transmissions permitted?
lines.a: Only on amateur frequencies above 222 MHz.

lines.text: What privileges are authorized in the US to persons holding an amateur service license granted by the government of Canada? The operating terms and conditions of the Canadian amateur service license, not to exceed US Amateur Extra class license privileges.
lines.q: What privileges are authorized in the US to persons holding an amateur service license granted by the government of Canada?
lines.a: The operating terms and conditions of the Canadian amateur service license, not to exceed US Amateur Extra class license privileges.

lines.text: Under what circumstances may a dealer sell an external RF power amplifier capable of operation below 144 MHz if it has not been granted FCC certification? The amplifier is constructed or modified by an amateur radio operator for use at an amateur station.
lines.q: Under what circumstances may a dealer sell an external RF power amplifier capable of operation below 144 MHz if it has not been granted FCC certification?
lines.a: The amplifier is constructed or modified by an amateur radio operator for use at an amateur station.

lines.text: Which of the following geographic descriptions approximately describes "Line A"? A line roughly parallel to and south of the border between the US and Canada.
lines.q: Which of the following geographic descriptions approximately describes "Line A"?
lines.a: A line roughly parallel to and south of the border between the US and Canada.

lines.text: Amateur stations may not transmit in which of the following frequency segments if they are located in the contiguous 48 states and north of Line A? 420 MHz - 430 MHz.
lines.q: Amateur stations may not transmit in which of the following frequency segments if they are located in the contiguous 48 states and north of Line A?
lines.a: 420 MHz - 430 MHz.

lines.text: Under what circumstances might the FCC issue a Special Temporary Authority (STA) to an amateur station? To provide for experimental amateur communications.
lines.q: Under what circumstances might the FCC issue a Special Temporary Authority (STA) to an amateur station?
lines.a: To provide for experimental amateur communications.

lines.text: When may an amateur station send a message to a business? When neither the amateur nor their employer has a pecuniary interest in the communications.
lines.q: When may an amateur station send a message to a business?
lines.a: When neither the amateur nor their employer has a pecuniary interest in the communications.

lines.text: Which of the following types of amateur station communications are prohibited? Communications transmitted for hire or material compensation, except as otherwise provided in the rules.
lines.q: Which of the following types of amateur station communications are prohibited?
lines.a: Communications transmitted for hire or material compensation, except as otherwise provided in the rules.

lines.text: Which of the following cannot be transmitted over an amateur radio mesh network? Messages encoded to obscure their meaning.
lines.q: Which of the following cannot be transmitted over an amateur radio mesh network?
lines.a: Messages encoded to obscure their meaning.

lines.text: Who may be the control operator of an auxiliary station? Only Technician, General, Advanced, or Amateur Extra class operators.
lines.q: Who may be the control operator of an auxiliary station?
lines.a: Only Technician, General, Advanced, or Amateur Extra class operators.

lines.text: Which of the following best describes one of the standards that must be met by an external RF power amplifier if it is to qualify for a grant of FCC certification? It must satisfy the FCC’s spurious emission standards when operated at the lesser of 1500 watts or its full output power.
lines.q: Which of the following best describes one of the standards that must be met by an external RF power amplifier if it is to qualify for a grant of FCC certification?
lines.a: It must satisfy the FCC’s spurious emission standards when operated at the lesser of 1500 watts or its full output power.

lines.q: What is the direction of an ascending pass for an amateur satellite?
lines.a: From south to north.

lines.q: How is an upload signal processed by an inverting linear transponder?
lines.a: The signal is mixed with a local oscillator signal and the difference product is transmitted.

lines.text: What is meant by the “mode” of an amateur radio satellite? The satellite’s uplink and downlink frequency bands.
lines.q: What is meant by the “mode” of an amateur radio satellite?
lines.a: The satellite’s uplink and downlink frequency bands.

lines.text: What do the letters in a satellite’s mode designator specify? The uplink and downlink frequency ranges.
lines.q: What do the letters in a satellite’s mode designator specify?
lines.a: The uplink and downlink frequency ranges.

lines.text: What are Keplerian elements? Parameters that define the orbit of a satellite.
lines.q: What are Keplerian elements?
lines.a: Parameters that define the orbit of a satellite.

lines.text: Which of the following types of signals can be relayed through a linear transponder? FM and CW; SSB and SSTV; PSK and packet; All these choices are correct.
lines.q: Which of the following types of signals can be relayed through a linear transponder?
lines.a: FM and CW; SSB and SSTV; PSK and packet; All these choices are correct.

lines.text: Why should effective radiated power (ERP) be limited to a satellite that uses a linear transponder? To avoid reducing the downlink power to all other users.
lines.q: Why should effective radiated power (ERP) be limited to a satellite that uses a linear transponder?
lines.a: To avoid reducing the downlink power to all other users.

lines.text: What do the terms “L band” and “S band” specify? The 23- and 13-centimeter bands.
lines.q: What do the terms “L band” and “S band” specify?
lines.a: The 23- and 13-centimeter bands.

lines.text: What type of satellite appears to stay in one position in the sky? Geostationary.
lines.q: What type of satellite appears to stay in one position in the sky?
lines.a: Geostationary.

lines.text: What type of antenna can be used to minimize the effects of spin modulation and Faraday rotation? A circularly polarized antenna.
lines.q: What type of antenna can be used to minimize the effects of spin modulation and Faraday rotation?
lines.a: A circularly polarized antenna.

lines.text: What is the purpose of digital store-and-forward functions on an amateur radio satellite? To hold digital messages in the satellite for later download.
lines.q: What is the purpose of digital store-and-forward functions on an amateur radio satellite?
lines.a: To hold digital messages in the satellite for later download.

lines.q: In digital television, what does a coding rate of 3/4 mean?
lines.a: 25% of the data sent is forward error correction data.

lines.q: How many horizontal lines make up a fast-scan (NTSC) television frame?

lines.a: Specific tone frequencies.

lines.a: No additional indicator is required.

lines.a: Frequencies shared with various unlicensed wireless data services.

lines.a: A digital modulation technique using subcarriers at frequencies chosen to avoid intersymbol interference.

lines.text: What is deviation ratio? The ratio of the maximum carrier frequency deviation to the highest audio modulating frequency.
lines.q: What is deviation ratio?
lines.a: The ratio of the maximum carrier frequency deviation to the highest audio modulating frequency.

lines.text: What is frequency division multiplexing (FDM)? Dividing the transmitted signal into separate frequency bands that each carry a different data stream.
lines.q: What is frequency division multiplexing (FDM)?
lines.a: Dividing the transmitted signal into separate frequency bands that each carry a different data stream.

lines.text: What is digital time division multiplexing? Two or more signals are arranged to share discrete time slots of a data transmission.
lines.q: What is digital time division multiplexing?
lines.a: Two or more signals are arranged to share discrete time slots of a data transmission.

lines.text: Group E8C.
What is Quadrature Amplitude Modulation or QAM? Transmission of data by modulating the amplitude of two carriers of the same frequency but 90 degrees out of phase.
lines.q: What is Quadrature Amplitude Modulation or QAM?
lines.a: Transmission of data by modulating the amplitude of two carriers of the same frequency but 90 degrees out of phase.

lines.text: What is the definition of symbol rate in a digital transmission? The rate at which the waveform changes to convey information.
lines.q: What is the definition of symbol rate in a digital transmission?
lines.a: The rate at which the waveform changes to convey information.

lines.text: Why should the phase of a PSK signal be changed at the zero crossing of the RF signal? To minimize bandwidth.
lines.q: Why should the phase of a PSK signal be changed at the zero crossing of the RF signal?
lines.a: To minimize bandwidth.

lines.text: What technique minimizes the bandwidth of a PSK31 signal? Use of sinusoidal data pulses.
lines.q: What technique minimizes the bandwidth of a PSK31 signal?
lines.a: Use of sinusoidal data pulses.

lines.text: What is the approximate bandwidth of a 13-WPM International Morse Code transmission? 52 Hz.
lines.q: What is the approximate bandwidth of a 13-WPM International Morse Code transmission?
lines.a: 52 Hz.

lines.text: What is the bandwidth of an FT8 signal? 50 Hz.
lines.q: What is the bandwidth of an FT8 signal?
lines.a: 50 Hz.

lines.text: What is the bandwidth of a 4,800-Hz frequency shift, 9,600-baud ASCII FM transmission? 15.36 kHz.
lines.q: What is the bandwidth of a 4,800-Hz frequency shift, 9,600-baud ASCII FM transmission?

lines.text: How does ARQ accomplish error correction? If errors are detected, a retransmission is requested.
lines.q: How does ARQ accomplish error correction?
lines.a: If errors are detected, a retransmission is requested.

lines.text: Which digital code allows only one bit to change between sequential code values? Gray code.
lines.q: Which digital code allows only one bit to change between sequential code values?
lines.a: Gray code.

lines.text: How can data rate be increased without increasing bandwidth? Using a more efficient digital code.
lines.q: How can data rate be increased without increasing bandwidth?
lines.a: Using a more efficient digital code.

lines.text: What is the relationship between symbol rate and baud? They are the same.
lines.q: What is the relationship between symbol rate and baud?
lines.a: They are the same.

lines.text: What factors affect the bandwidth of a transmitted CW signal? Keying speed and shape factor (rise and fall time).
lines.q: What factors affect the bandwidth of a transmitted CW signal?
lines.a: Keying speed and shape factor (rise and fall time).

lines.text: What is described by the constellation diagram of a QAM or QPSK signal? The possible phase and amplitude states for each symbol.
lines.q: What is described by the constellation diagram of a QAM or QPSK signal?
lines.a: The possible phase and amplitude states for each symbol.

lines.text: What type of addresses do nodes have in a mesh network? Internet Protocol (IP).
lines.q: What type of addresses do nodes have in a mesh network?
lines.a: Internet Protocol (IP).

lines.text: What technique do individual nodes use to form a mesh network? Discovery and link establishment protocols.
lines.q: What technique do individual nodes use to form a mesh network?
lines.a: Discovery and link establishment protocols.

lines.text: Group E8D.
Why are received spread spectrum signals resistant to interference? Signals not using the spread spectrum algorithm are suppressed in the receiver.
lines.q: Why are received spread spectrum signals resistant to interference?
lines.a: Signals not using the spread spectrum algorithm are suppressed in the receiver.

lines.text: What spread spectrum communications technique uses a high-speed binary bit stream to shift the phase of an RF carrier? Direct sequence.
lines.q: What spread spectrum communications technique uses a high-speed binary bit stream to shift the phase of an RF carrier?
lines.a: Direct sequence.

lines.text: Which describes spread spectrum frequency hopping? Rapidly varying the frequency of a transmitted signal according to a pseudorandom sequence.
lines.q: Which describes spread spectrum frequency hopping?
lines.a: Rapidly varying the frequency of a transmitted signal according to a pseudorandom sequence.

lines.text: What is the primary effect of extremely short rise or fall time on a CW signal? The generation of key clicks.
lines.q: What is the primary effect of extremely short rise or fall time on a CW signal?
lines.a: The generation of key clicks.

lines.text: What is the most common method of reducing key clicks? Increase keying waveform rise and fall times.
lines.q: What is the most common method of reducing key clicks?
lines.a: Increase keying waveform rise and fall times.

lines.text: What is the advantage of including parity bits in ASCII characters? Some types of errors can be detected.
lines.q: What is the advantage of including parity bits in ASCII characters?
lines.a: Some types of errors can be detected.

lines.text: What is a common cause of overmodulation of AFSK signals? Excessive transmit audio levels.
lines.q: What is a common cause of overmodulation of AFSK signals?
lines.a: Excessive transmit audio levels.

lines.text: What parameter evaluates distortion of an AFSK signal caused by excessive input audio levels? Intermodulation Distortion (IMD).
lines.q: What parameter evaluates distortion of an AFSK signal caused by excessive input audio levels?
lines.a: Intermodulation Distortion (IMD).

lines.text: What is considered an acceptable maximum IMD level for an idling PSK signal? -30 dB.
lines.q: What is considered an acceptable maximum IMD level for an idling PSK signal?

lines.text: What are some of the differences between the Baudot digital code and ASCII? Baudot uses 5 data bits per character, ASCII uses 7 or 8; Baudot uses 2 characters as letters/figures shift codes, ASCII has no letters/figures shift code.
lines.q: What are some of the differences between the Baudot digital code and ASCII?
lines.a: Baudot uses 5 data bits per character, ASCII uses 7 or 8; Baudot uses 2 characters as letters/figures shift codes, ASCII has no letters/figures shift code.

lines.text: What is one advantage of using ASCII code for data communications? It is possible to transmit both uppercase and lowercase text.
lines.q: What is one advantage of using ASCII code for data communications?
lines.a: It is possible to transmit both uppercase and lowercase text.

lines.text: Extra answers. E9 - Antennas and Transmission Lines.
Group E9A.
What is an isotropic radiator? A hypothetical, lossless antenna having equal radiation intensity in all directions used as a reference for antenna gain.
lines.q: What is an isotropic radiator?
lines.a: A hypothetical, lossless antenna having equal radiation intensity in all directions used as a reference for antenna gain.

lines.text: What is the effective radiated power (ERP) of a repeater station with 150 watts transmitter power output, 2 dB feed line loss, 2.2 dB duplexer loss, and 7 dBd antenna gain? 286 watts.
lines.q: What is the effective radiated power (ERP) of a repeater station with 150 watts transmitter power output, 2 dB feed line loss, 2.2 dB duplexer loss, and 7 dBd antenna gain?
lines.a: 286 watts.

lines.text: What term describing total radiated power takes into account all gains and losses? Effective radiated power.
lines.q: What term describing total radiated power takes into account all gains and losses?
lines.a: Effective radiated power.

lines.text: Which of the following factors affect the feed point impedance of an antenna? Antenna height.
lines.q: Which of the following factors affect the feed point impedance of an antenna?
lines.a: Antenna height.

lines.text: What does the term “ground gain” mean? An increase in signal strength from ground reflections in the environment of the antenna.
lines.q: What does the term “ground gain” mean?
lines.a: An increase in signal strength from ground reflections in the environment of the antenna.

lines.text: What is the effective radiated power (ERP) of a repeater station with 200 watts transmitter power output, 4 dB feed line loss, 3.2 dB duplexer loss, 0.8 dB circulator loss, and 10 dBd antenna gain? 317 watts.
lines.q: What is the effective radiated power (ERP) of a repeater station with 200 watts transmitter power output, 4 dB feed line loss, 3.2 dB duplexer loss, 0.8 dB circulator loss, and 10 dBd antenna gain?
lines.a: 317 watts.

lines.text: What is the effective isotropic radiated power (EIRP) of a repeater station with 200 watts transmitter power output, 2 dB feed line loss, 2.8 dB duplexer loss, 1.2 dB circulator loss, and 7 dBi antenna gain? 252 watts.
lines.q: What is the effective isotropic radiated power (EIRP) of a repeater station with 200 watts transmitter power output, 2 dB feed line loss, 2.8 dB duplexer loss, 1.2 dB circulator loss, and 7 dBi antenna gain?
lines.a: 252 watts.

lines.text: Which frequency band has the smallest first Fresnel zone? 5.8 GHz.
lines.q: Which frequency band has the smallest first Fresnel zone?
lines.a: 5.8 GHz.

lines.text: What is antenna efficiency? Radiation resistance divided by total resistance.
lines.q: What is antenna efficiency?
lines.a: Radiation resistance divided by total resistance.

lines.text: Which of the following improves the efficiency of a ground-mounted quarter-wave vertical antenna? Installing a ground radial system.
lines.q: Which of the following improves the efficiency of a ground-mounted quarter-wave vertical antenna?
lines.a: Installing a ground radial system.

lines.text: Which of the following determines ground losses for a ground-mounted vertical antenna operating on HF? Soil conductivity.
lines.q: Which of the following determines ground losses for a ground-mounted vertical antenna operating on HF?
lines.a: Soil conductivity.

lines.text: How much gain does an antenna have compared to a half-wavelength dipole if it has 6 dB gain over an isotropic radiator? 3.85 dB.
lines.q: How much gain does an antenna have compared to a half-wavelength dipole if it has 6 dB gain over an isotropic radiator?

lines.text: Group E9B.
What is the difference in radiated power between a lossless antenna with gain and an isotropic radiator driven by the same power? They are the same.
lines.q: What is the difference in radiated power between a lossless antenna with gain and an isotropic radiator driven by the same power?
lines.a: They are the same.

lines.text: What is the far field of an antenna? The region where the shape of the radiation pattern no longer varies with distance.
lines.q: What is the far field of an antenna?
lines.a: The region where the shape of the radiation pattern no longer varies with distance.

lines.text: What type of analysis is commonly used for modeling antennas? Method of Moments.
lines.q: What type of analysis is commonly used for modeling antennas?
lines.a: Method of Moments.

lines.text: What is the principle of a Method of Moments analysis? A wire is modeled as a series of segments, each having a uniform value of current.
lines.q: What is the principle of a Method of Moments analysis?
lines.a: A wire is modeled as a series of segments, each having a uniform value of current.

lines.text: What is a disadvantage of decreasing the number of wire segments in an antenna model below 10 segments per half-wavelength? The computed feed point impedance may be incorrect.
lines.q: What is a disadvantage of decreasing the number of wire segments in an antenna model below 10 segments per half-wavelength?
lines.a: The computed feed point impedance may be incorrect.

lines.text: Group E9C.
What type of radiation pattern is created by two 1/4-wavelength vertical antennas spaced 1/2-wavelength apart and fed 180 degrees out of phase? A figure-eight oriented along the axis of the array.
lines.q: What type of radiation pattern is created by two 1/4-wavelength vertical antennas spaced 1/2-wavelength apart and fed 180 degrees out of phase?
lines.a: A figure-eight oriented along the axis of the array.

lines.text: What type of radiation pattern is created by two 1/4-wavelength vertical antennas spaced 1/4-wavelength apart and fed 90 degrees out of phase? Cardioid.
lines.q: What type of radiation pattern is created by two 1/4-wavelength vertical antennas spaced 1/4-wavelength apart and fed 90 degrees out of phase?
lines.a: Cardioid.

lines.text: What type of radiation pattern is created by two 1/4-wavelength vertical antennas spaced 1/2-wavelength apart and fed in phase? A figure-eight broadside to the axis of the array.
lines.q: What type of radiation pattern is created by two 1/4-wavelength vertical antennas spaced 1/2-wavelength apart and fed in phase?
lines.a: A figure-eight broadside to the axis of the array.

lines.text: What happens to the radiation pattern of an unterminated long wire antenna as the wire length is increased? Additional lobes form with major lobes increasingly aligned with the axis of the antenna.
lines.q: What happens to the radiation pattern of an unterminated long wire antenna as the wire length is increased?
lines.a: Additional lobes form with major lobes increasingly aligned with the axis of the antenna.

lines.text: What is the purpose of feeding an off-center-fed dipole (OCFD) between the center and one end instead of at the midpoint? To create a similar feed point impedance on multiple bands.
lines.q: What is the purpose of feeding an off-center-fed dipole (OCFD) between the center and one end instead of at the midpoint?
lines.a: To create a similar feed point impedance on multiple bands.

lines.text: What is the effect of adding a terminating resistor to a rhombic or long-wire antenna? It changes the radiation pattern from bidirectional to unidirectional.
lines.q: What is the effect of adding a terminating resistor to a rhombic or long-wire antenna?
lines.a: It changes the radiation pattern from bidirectional to unidirectional.

lines.text: What is the approximate feed point impedance at the center of a two-wire half-wave folded dipole antenna? 300 ohms.
lines.q: What is the approximate feed point impedance at the center of a two-wire half-wave folded dipole antenna?
lines.a: 300 ohms.

lines.text: What is a folded dipole antenna? A half-wave dipole with an additional parallel wire connecting its two ends.
lines.q: What is a folded dipole antenna?
lines.a: A half-wave dipole with an additional parallel wire connecting its two ends.

lines.text: Which of the following describes a G5RV antenna? A wire antenna center-fed through a specific length of open-wire line connected to a balun and coaxial feed line.
lines.q: Which of the following describes a G5RV antenna?
lines.a: A wire antenna center-fed through a specific length of open-wire line connected to a balun and coaxial feed line.

lines.text: Which of the following describes a Zepp antenna? An end-fed half-wavelength dipole.
lines.q: Which of the following describes a Zepp antenna?
lines.a: An end-fed half-wavelength dipole.

lines.text: How is the far-field elevation pattern of a vertically polarized antenna affected by being mounted over seawater versus soil? Radiation at low angles increases.
lines.q: How is the far-field elevation pattern of a vertically polarized antenna affected by being mounted over seawater versus soil?
lines.a: Radiation at low angles increases.

lines.text: Which of the following describes an extended double Zepp antenna? A center-fed 1.25-wavelength dipole antenna.
lines.q: Which of the following describes an extended double Zepp antenna?
lines.a: A center-fed 1.25-wavelength dipole antenna.

lines.text: How does the radiation pattern of a horizontally polarized antenna vary with increasing height above ground? The takeoff angle of the lowest elevation lobe decreases.
lines.q: How does the radiation pattern of a horizontally polarized antenna vary with increasing height above ground?
lines.a: The takeoff angle of the lowest elevation lobe decreases.

lines.text: How does the radiation pattern of a horizontally-polarized antenna mounted above a long slope compare with the same antenna mounted above flat ground? The main lobe takeoff angle decreases in the downhill direction.
lines.q: How does the radiation pattern of a horizontally-polarized antenna mounted above a long slope compare with the same antenna mounted above flat ground?
lines.a: The main lobe takeoff angle decreases in the downhill direction.

lines.text: Group E9D.
How much does the gain of an ideal parabolic reflector antenna increase when the operating frequency is doubled? 6 dB.
lines.q: How much does the gain of an ideal parabolic reflector antenna increase when the operating frequency is doubled?
lines.a: 6 dB.

lines.text: How can two linearly polarized Yagi antennas be used to produce circular polarization? Arrange two Yagis on the same axis and perpendicular to each other with the driven elements at the same point on the boom and fed 90 degrees out of phase.
lines.q: How can two linearly polarized Yagi antennas be used to produce circular polarization?
lines.a: Arrange two Yagis on the same axis and perpendicular to each other with the driven elements at the same point on the boom and fed 90 degrees out of phase.

lines.text: What is the most efficient location for a loading coil on an electrically short whip? Near the center of the vertical radiator.
lines.q: What is the most efficient location for a loading coil on an electrically short whip?
lines.a: Near the center of the vertical radiator.

lines.text: Why should antenna loading coils have a high ratio of reactance to resistance? To maximize efficiency.
lines.q: Why should antenna loading coils have a high ratio of reactance to resistance?
lines.a: To maximize efficiency.

lines.text: Approximately how long is a Yagi’s driven element? 1/2 wavelength.
lines.q: Approximately how long is a Yagi’s driven element?
lines.a: 1/2 wavelength.

lines.text: What happens to SWR bandwidth when one or more loading coils are used to resonate an electrically short antenna? It is decreased.
lines.q: What happens to SWR bandwidth when one or more loading coils are used to resonate an electrically short antenna?
lines.a: It is decreased.

lines.text: What is an advantage of top loading an electrically short HF vertical antenna? Improved radiation efficiency.
lines.q: What is an advantage of top loading an electrically short HF vertical antenna?
lines.a: Improved radiation efficiency.

lines.text: What happens as the Q of an antenna increases? SWR bandwidth decreases.
lines.q: What happens as the Q of an antenna increases?
lines.a: SWR bandwidth decreases.

lines.text: What is the function of a loading coil in an electrically short antenna? To resonate the antenna by cancelling the capacitive reactance.
lines.q: What is the function of a loading coil in an electrically short antenna?
lines.a: To resonate the antenna by cancelling the capacitive reactance.

lines.text: How does radiation resistance of a base-fed whip antenna change below its resonant frequency? Radiation resistance decreases.
lines.q: How does radiation resistance of a base-fed whip antenna change below its resonant frequency?
lines.a: Radiation resistance decreases.

lines.text: Why do most two-element Yagis with normal spacing have a reflector instead of a director? Higher gain.
lines.q: Why do most two-element Yagis with normal spacing have a reflector instead of a director?
lines.a: Higher gain.

lines.text: What is the purpose of making a Yagi’s parasitic elements either longer or shorter than resonance? Control of phase shift.
lines.q: What is the purpose of making a Yagi’s parasitic elements either longer or shorter than resonance?
lines.a: Control of phase shift.

lines.text: Group E9E.
Which matching system for Yagi antennas requires the driven element to be insulated from the boom? Beta or hairpin.
lines.q: Which matching system for Yagi antennas requires the driven element to be insulated from the boom?
lines.a: Beta or hairpin.

lines.text: What antenna matching system matches coaxial cable to an antenna by connecting the shield to the center of the antenna and the conductor a fraction of a wavelength to one side? Gamma match.
lines.q: What antenna matching system matches coaxial cable to an antenna by connecting the shield to the center of the antenna and the conductor a fraction of a wavelength to one side?
lines.a: Gamma match.

lines.text: What matching system uses a short length of transmission line connected in parallel with the feed line at or near the feed point? Stub match.
lines.q: What matching system uses a short length of transmission line connected in parallel with the feed line at or near the feed point?
lines.a: Stub match.

lines.text: What is the purpose of the series capacitor in a gamma match? To cancel unwanted inductive reactance.
lines.q: What is the purpose of the series capacitor in a gamma match?
lines.a: To cancel unwanted inductive reactance.

lines.text: What Yagi driven element feed point impedance is required to use a beta or hairpin matching system? Capacitive (driven element electrically shorter than 1/2 wavelength).
lines.q: What Yagi driven element feed point impedance is required to use a beta or hairpin matching system?
lines.a: Capacitive (driven element electrically shorter than 1/2 wavelength).

lines.text: Which of these transmission line impedances would be suitable for constructing a quarter-wave Q-section for matching a 100-ohm feed point impedance to a 50-ohm transmission line? 75 ohms.
lines.q: Which of these transmission line impedances would be suitable for constructing a quarter-wave Q-section for matching a 100-ohm feed point impedance to a 50-ohm transmission line?
lines.a: 75 ohms.

lines.text: What parameter describes the interaction of a load and transmission line? Reflection coefficient.
lines.q: What parameter describes the interaction of a load and transmission line?
lines.a: Reflection coefficient.

lines.text: What is a use for a Wilkinson divider? To divide power equally between two 50-ohm loads while maintaining 50-ohm input impedance.
lines.q: What is a use for a Wilkinson divider?
lines.a: To divide power equally between two 50-ohm loads while maintaining 50-ohm input impedance.

lines.text: Which of the following is used to shunt feed a grounded tower at its base? Gamma match.
lines.q: Which of the following is used to shunt feed a grounded tower at its base?
lines.a: Gamma match.

lines.text: What is the purpose of using multiple driven elements connected through phasing lines? To control the antenna’s radiation pattern.
lines.q: What is the purpose of using multiple driven elements connected through phasing lines?
lines.a: To control the antenna’s radiation pattern.

lines.text: Group E9F.
What is the velocity factor of a transmission line? The velocity of a wave in the transmission line divided by the velocity of light in a vacuum.
lines.q: What is the velocity factor of a transmission line?
lines.a: The velocity of a wave in the transmission line divided by the velocity of light in a vacuum.

lines.text: Which of the following has the biggest effect on the velocity factor of a transmission line? The insulating dielectric material.
lines.q: Which of the following has the biggest effect on the velocity factor of a transmission line?
lines.a: The insulating dielectric material.

lines.text: Why is the electrical length of a coaxial cable longer than its physical length? Electromagnetic waves move more slowly in a coaxial cable than in air.
lines.q: Why is the electrical length of a coaxial cable longer than its physical length?
lines.a: Electromagnetic waves move more slowly in a coaxial cable than in air.

lines.text: What impedance does a 1/2-wavelength transmission line present to an RF generator when the line is shorted at the far end? Very low impedance.
lines.q: What impedance does a 1/2-wavelength transmission line present to an RF generator when the line is shorted at the far end?
lines.a: Very low impedance.

lines.text: What is microstrip? Precision printed circuit conductors above a ground plane that provide constant impedance interconnects at microwave frequencies.
lines.q: What is microstrip?
lines.a: Precision printed circuit conductors above a ground plane that provide constant impedance interconnects at microwave frequencies.

lines.text: What is the approximate physical length of an air-insulated, parallel conductor transmission line that is electrically 1/2 wavelength long at 14.10 MHz? 10.6 meters.
lines.q: What is the approximate physical length of an air-insulated, parallel conductor transmission line that is electrically 1/2 wavelength long at 14.10 MHz?
lines.a: 10.6 meters.

lines.text: How does parallel conductor transmission line compare to coaxial cable with a plastic dielectric? Lower loss.
lines.q: How does parallel conductor transmission line compare to coaxial cable with a plastic dielectric?
lines.a: Lower loss.

lines.text: Which of the following is a significant difference between foam dielectric coaxial cable and solid dielectric coaxial cable, assuming all other parameters are the same? Foam dielectric coaxial cable has lower safe maximum operating voltage; Foam dielectric coaxial cable has lower loss per unit of length; Foam dielectric coaxial cable has higher velocity factor; All these choices are correct.
lines.q: Which of the following is a significant difference between foam dielectric coaxial cable and solid dielectric coaxial cable, assuming all other parameters are the same?
lines.a: Foam dielectric coaxial cable has lower safe maximum operating voltage; Foam dielectric coaxial cable has lower loss per unit of length; Foam dielectric coaxial cable has higher velocity factor; All these choices are correct.

lines.text: What impedance does a 1/4-wavelength transmission line present to an RF generator when the line is shorted at the far end? Very high impedance.
lines.q: What impedance does a 1/4-wavelength transmission line present to an RF generator when the line is shorted at the far end?
lines.a: Very high impedance.

lines.text: What impedance does a 1/8-wavelength transmission line present to an RF generator when the line is shorted at the far end? An inductive reactance.
lines.q: What impedance does a 1/8-wavelength transmission line present to an RF generator when the line is shorted at the far end?
lines.a: An inductive reactance.

lines.text: What impedance does a 1/8-wavelength transmission line present to an RF generator when the line is open at the far end? A capacitive reactance.
lines.q: What impedance does a 1/8-wavelength transmission line present to an RF generator when the line is open at the far end?
lines.a: A capacitive reactance.

lines.text: What impedance does a 1/4-wavelength transmission line present to an RF generator when the line is open at the far end? Very low impedance.
lines.q: What impedance does a 1/4-wavelength transmission line present to an RF generator when the line is open at the far end?
lines.a: Very low impedance.

lines.text: Group E9G.
Which of the following can be calculated using a Smith chart? Impedance along transmission lines.
lines.q: Which of the following can be calculated using a Smith chart?
lines.a: Impedance along transmission lines.

lines.text: What type of coordinate system is used in a Smith chart? Resistance circles and reactance arcs.
lines.q: What type of coordinate system is used in a Smith chart?
lines.a: Resistance circles and reactance arcs.

lines.text: Which of the following is often determined using a Smith chart? Impedance and SWR values in transmission lines.
lines.q: Which of the following is often determined using a Smith chart?
lines.a: Impedance and SWR values in transmission lines.

lines.text: What are the two families of circles and arcs that make up a Smith chart? Resistance and reactance.
lines.q: What are the two families of circles and arcs that make up a Smith chart?
lines.a: Resistance and reactance.

lines.text: Which of the following is a common use for a Smith chart? Determine the length and position of an impedance matching stub.
lines.q: Which of the following is a common use for a Smith chart?
lines.a: Determine the length and position of an impedance matching stub.

lines.text: How is a Smith chart normalized? Reassign the prime center’s impedance value.
lines.q: How is a Smith chart normalized?
lines.a: Reassign the prime center’s impedance value.

lines.text: What third family of circles is often added to a Smith chart during the process of designing impedance matching networks? Constant-SWR circles.
lines.q: What third family of circles is often added to a Smith chart during the process of designing impedance matching networks?
lines.a: Constant-SWR circles.

lines.text: What do the arcs on a Smith chart represent? Points with constant reactance.
lines.q: What do the arcs on a Smith chart represent?
lines.a: Points with constant reactance.

lines.text: In what units are the wavelength scales on a Smith chart calibrated? In fractions of transmission line electrical wavelength.
lines.q: In what units are the wavelength scales on a Smith chart calibrated?
lines.a: In fractions of transmission line electrical wavelength.

lines.text: Group E9H.
When constructing a Beverage antenna, which of the following factors should be included in the design to achieve good performance at the desired frequency? It should be at least one wavelength long.
lines.q: When constructing a Beverage antenna, which of the following factors should be included in the design to achieve good performance at the desired frequency?
lines.a: It should be at least one wavelength long.

lines.text: Which is generally true for 160- and 80-meter receiving antennas? Atmospheric noise is so high that directivity is much more important than losses.
lines.q: Which is generally true for 160- and 80-meter receiving antennas?
lines.a: Atmospheric noise is so high that directivity is much more important than losses.

lines.text: What is receiving directivity factor (RDF)? Peak antenna gain compared to average gain over the hemisphere around and above the antenna.
lines.q: What is receiving directivity factor (RDF)?
lines.a: Peak antenna gain compared to average gain over the hemisphere around and above the antenna.

lines.text: What is the purpose of placing an electrostatic shield around a small-loop direction-finding antenna? It eliminates unbalanced capacitive coupling to the antenna’s surroundings, improving the depth of its nulls.
lines.q: What is the purpose of placing an electrostatic shield around a small-loop direction-finding antenna?
lines.a: It eliminates unbalanced capacitive coupling to the antenna’s surroundings, improving the depth of its nulls.

lines.text: What challenge is presented by a small wire-loop antenna for direction finding? It has a bidirectional null pattern.
lines.q: What challenge is presented by a small wire-loop antenna for direction finding?
lines.a: It has a bidirectional null pattern.

lines.text: What indicates the correct value of terminating resistance for a Beverage antenna? Minimum variation in SWR over the desired frequency range.
lines.q: What indicates the correct value of terminating resistance for a Beverage antenna?
lines.a: Minimum variation in SWR over the desired frequency range.

lines.text: What is the function of a Beverage antenna’s termination resistor? Absorb signals from the reverse direction.
lines.q: What is the function of a Beverage antenna’s termination resistor?
lines.a: Absorb signals from the reverse direction.

lines.text: What is the function of a sense antenna? It modifies the pattern of a DF antenna to provide a null in only one direction.
lines.q: What is the function of a sense antenna?
